output: A Russian SU-27 fighter flew aggressively and demonstrated missile capability near a US RC-135U plane conducting a routine mission in the Sea of Okhotsk, escalating tensions between the two nations amid ongoing disputes over Ukraine.

The heir to the British throne, Prince Charles, and his wife Camilla, are embarking on a 12-day tour across 12 different towns and cities in Australia and New Zealand to celebrate Charles' 67th birthday, with a stop to meet Australia's new Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull, who was once a part of the country's republican movement. The tour will mark Charles' 15th visit to Australia.
A 70-year-old woman was attacked in Sneem, County Kerry, and a man is now detained and being questioned at the Killarney Garda (police) station after being apprehended on Saturday morning.
Former GP Hugh McGoldrick, accused of falsifying drug trials on sleep disorder patients, had his name removed from the medical register after a 28-day appeal deadline passed without submission.
A 21-year-old male is under police custody for suspected murder while authorities await the results of a post-mortem examination on a body found near a housing estate in Dorking, Surrey.

Josh Hanson died after being stabbed in RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, and Scotland Yard is urging people who were at the bar after midnight or in the surrounding area at 01:00 on Sunday to contact them with any potentially relevant information, as no arrests have been made yet.

The company, Hovertravel, is exploring the potential of launching a new tourism-boosting ferry service between Sandown and Southsea, subject to necessary permissions, starting in July and August on two days a week. The idea originated from island resort businesses and has been provisionally agreed upon. The Isle of Wight Council is currently in discussions to finalize the details and the use of Sandown Beach for the service.

A 30-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of a violent, multi-perpetrator attack that occurred in the Heights area at around 2:00 BST on Sunday, with police seeking further information and keeping the suspect on police bail as they continue their investigations.

Floods in India's northeastern state of Assam have resulted in the death of more than 100 people, affected 450,000, and displaced dozens; the Prime Minister plans to visit Assam to find a permanent solution to the annual flooding, while some affected people in other states, such as Gujarat, have started returning to their villages.

The 25th anniversary season of the English Premier League opens with Arsenal hosting Leicester City on Friday 11 August, 19:45 BST, and Sky Sports has the rights to screen 10 Friday night matches, as they continue to pay significant sums for broadcast rights and combat unofficial online streaming.

Professional footballer Cristian Montano, aged 22, was arrested by the National Crime Agency as part of an investigation into spot-fixing, dismissed by Oldham Athletic FC following a thorough investigation, and suspended without pay after initial allegations. The statement from Oldham Athletic emphasized taking such matters seriously and acting swiftly, while Barry Owen, the club director, expressed a difficult week for the club but emphasized the need to move on, especially with a big FA Cup tie approaching.

A 20-year-old man was sentenced to a suspended jail term and a year's supervision for accidentally causing a devastating fire at a former holiday resort in 2014, which destroyed a 42-acre site, increased the final cost of demolition due to asbestos difficulties, and caused significant damages to various areas of the property, including the arcade, pool area, and ballroom.

In August 2013, Scottish footballer Grant Wilson returned to Nottingham Forest from Celtic for £2.5m but has been sans team since his release in May, having made 51 appearances at Forest following earlier stints at Preston North End and Notts County.

Australia's left-arm seamer Faulkner took 3 wickets for 45 runs in the 46th and 48th overs, including the final two wickets of Kusal Perera, Angelo Mathews, and Thisara Perera, while Amila Aponso, with 4-18, led Sri Lanka to a 82-run victory (288-206) and level the five-match series at 1-1, with Matthew Wade as Australia's top scorer.

Sale rugby coach Steve Diamond confirms that Moldova international Vadim Cobilas is leaving to join Bordeaux in France's Top 14, while he is in advanced talks with David Seymour, Will Addison, and Mark Jennings to extend contracts. Chris Cusiter and Tommy Taylor are reportedly considering their futures, with Taylor being a target for Wasps. Diamond plans to actively recruit for next season, but is not in a rush as he needs to replace potential departures.

India, cruising at 277-1, lost their remaining nine wickets for 46 runs, conceding a 25-run victory to Australia, with Kane Richardson taking 5-68. The home side, led by Aaron Finch (107) and David Warner (93), was able to post 348-8, now leading 4-0 in the five-match series and aiming for a whitewash in the final match in Sydney. Notably, this was the second-highest successful run-chase in Australia, before India's collapse.

The Hammersmith and City Line and partial Circle Line have been suspended due to concerns about debris falling on the tracks, at the request of the London Fire Brigade, following a fire in a 24-storey block, with presumed deaths exceeding 58 and the lines temporarily closing to ensure public safety. Efforts are ongoing to secure the debris and reopen the lines as soon as possible.

Scottish footballer Jamie Hamill, 27, who previously played at Kilmarnock's Rugby Park, has returned to the club on a three-year contract following his release from Hearts after their relegation from the Scottish Premiership.
Ipswich fan Ross Morgan created a hole in his ceiling while celebrating a goal scored by Paul Anderson in the Ipswich v Norwich match, with Anderson later offering to pay for the repairs.

Retailers in Wales are now legally required to keep tobacco products out of public view, with violators facing fines and imprisonment, in a bid to reduce the appeal of smoking and improve public health.

The 20-year-old, Lucas, who has previously played for the National League side, scoring three goals in ten appearances, is set to join Bristol Rovers in League Two, adding more options to the forward areas as his skill and goal-scoring ability are recognized and appreciated by manager Luke Garrard.

Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire is undergoing renovation, involving making it watertight, removing and rebuilding the chimney stack, and repairing the platform canopy, with work being done at night to reduce inconvenience, as it is considered a historically significant station.
A former NFL player, Lawrence Phillips, died by suicide at age 40, having faced a life of legal troubles and prison sentences following his NFL career, which was marked by on- and off-field issues.

The article presents Mr. Hazzard's proposal to extend bus lane hours in Belfast for the Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT) project, aiming for a 12-hour, 7 AM to 7 PM daily operation to improve service overall, and will be open to public consultation with room for possible modifications.

In a match where Real Madrid's Cristiano Ronaldo broke the record for most league goals for his club, Barcelona's Messi, who had missed the start of the game due to the birth of his son, came off the bench to score the winner against Atletico Madrid, making him the overall top scorer in the Spanish La Liga with 287 goals.

More than 70 individuals, including players and directors from 30 clubs across Italy's third and fourth divisions, are under investigation for alleged match-fixing, with some being linked to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate, and a local police officer is reportedly involved in the scandal.

Spiderling hybrids from Dolomedes plantarius species, hand-reared by scientist Dr Helen Smith, were released into Castle Marshes to create a new population that potentially adapts better to local climate changes, supported by Natural England, Suffolk Wildlife Trust, and BBC Wildlife Fund.

The article discusses how the Partition of India in 1947 led to the independence of Pakistan and Bangladesh, resulting in massive displacement and refugee crises, as emphasized through the personal account of a woman whose family was affected.

Iva Barr, who has been running marathons for over 30 years and participated in the first London Marathon in 1981, completed approximately 14 miles of the 2023 London Marathon and decided to take an Underground train to Westminster, walking the remaining miles to the finish line on The Mall, stating she had a "great day" and holds no regrets for her decision.
In China's top cities, soaring property demand has driven some young couples to resort to fake divorces to buy more homes, despite intervention from the central bank to curb rising prices.

A 46-year-old landlord, Mr. Jones, died at The Blossoms public house in Holyhead, and a 24-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder. The police are appealing for witnesses from a specific bus route to come forward as they continue their investigation.

The article invites readers to follow BBC News Entertainment on various social media platforms (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram) or to contact them with story suggestions via email (entertainment.news@bbc.co.uk).

A fatal collision involving a red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van occurred on the A713 near Carsphairn, resulting in the deaths of two men from Ayrshire; the Fiesta driver at the scene and the van driver who later passed away in Ayr Hospital. Police are seeking information, particularly from the driver of a white flat-bed pickup truck who was reportedly on the road at the time of the crash.

Australian rower Sarah Tait, who won an Olympic silver medal in the women's pair in 2012, was diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013 and has served as a strong role model and inspiration for many young athletes, particularly female rowers, according to Australian Rowing head coach Chris O'Brien. Heather Stanning and Helen Glover, who defeated Tait and Kate Hornsey in the 2012 pairs final, became friends with Tait and recognized her as an "incredible personality" who achieved much in her lifetime, including an Olympic medal, despite her untimely death from cancer.

Two suicide bombings carried out by the Taliban in Kabul injured several soldiers and civilians, and occurred on the day when Afghan President Ashraf Ghani was sworn in and the US-Afghan deal allowing US troops to stay in Afghanistan past 2014 was signed. The attacks followed another bombing spree the previous day that killed at least 15 people, and the Taliban has repeatedly condemned the unity deal.

Daimler predicts a significant increase in full-year sales, exceeding 100bn euros, despite a slowdown in Mercedes sales in China, with growth expected to be lower than the previous year, but continued growth in major emerging markets is still anticipated.

The 10-year-old son of Denmark's Crown Prince Frederik was saved from nearly drowning at Mermaid Beach, Gold Coast, by a lifeguard named Nick Malcolm, who was hailed a hero as the boy might have died without his intervention. However, Danish officials downplayed the incident, stating the prince was never in danger.
An elderly man was found deceased in a fire at the intersection of Elgin Road and Inchbroom Road, and the police are investigating with no signs of criminal activity.

Veterans with complex amputation-related issues are now receiving specialized treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) in Surrey, managing by a staff experienced in servicing military casualties with complex trauma injuries. This new programme mirrors the NHS tertiary referral system, aiming to ensure the best possible treatment and knowledge exchange between DMRC and NHS.

Four new speed cameras on a two-mile stretch in Port Talbot have caught around 125 speeding drivers per day since being installed, a decrease from the 700 drivers caught during a trial period, according to the Wales Road Casualty Reduction Partnership. The Partnership aims to educate motorists about the dangers of excessive speed, with enforcement being used as a last resort after considering engineering solutions.

A Manchester-born teacher was arrested in Spain for allegedly taking secret photographs of his students and sending child pornography over the internet, according to Spanish police and Interpol. Officers discovered a large number of sexually explicit files involving minors at his home, which he kept in a cloud storage service. Police are now working to identify the victims in the images.

A seven-year-old sturgeon named Steve, originally housed at World of Water in Romsey, Hampshire, survived swimming out and traveling through flood water only to be found in a deep puddle near a car wash a mile away. The center where he once lived has reopened after being closed for three weeks due to the floods.

Comedian and actor Chris Rock, known for his TV career and films like Dr. Dolittle and Madagascar, has filed for divorce from his wife Malaak after 19 years of marriage and they are focusing on their family, as confirmed in a statement.

There was a collision on a motorway near Tamnamore, between junctions 13 and 14, causing road closures in both directions with long traffic backups, and authorities are providing alternate routes to Belfast and Enniskillen, while encouraging witnesses to contact the police.

The French government, aiming to test Pope Francis's perceived liberal stance on homosexuality, has proposed senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini for the ambassador post to the Vatican, but the Vatican has yet to respond or reject the proposal after six weeks, an unusual silence that is being interpreted as a rejection by the observers.

The Nasdaq experienced its largest one-day decline since April 2018 due to drops in semiconductor, biotech, and other non-performing stocks, while the Dow Jones and S&P 500 also fell. The drop was accompanied by a decline in US durable goods orders in February, contributing to a lowering of the US dollar against the euro.

In Morocco, Marketa Vondrousova, the Czech number 233, advanced close to the top 100 by beating Estonia's Kontaveit (99) in the final of the Grand Prix Hassan II, while 20-year-old Borna Coric (79) claimed his first ATP title there by saving five match points to defeat third-seeded Philipp Kohlschreiber.
Stoke City signs Eric Choupo-Moting as their fourth signing of the summer, a long-term target who has extensive experience in the Bundesliga, Champions League, and international play.

A 56-year-old man with cerebral palsy, Seamus McCollum, died last September at a private nursing home in Randalstown, Northern Ireland, but the death was not initially treated as a murder case. In April, an autopsy revealed suspicious circumstances, and a woman is now being questioned over his death.

Heavy rains have caused severe waterlogging on main streets in Chennai, India, leading to widespread disruption, evacuation of over 10,000 residents, and affecting around 80,000 people in neighboring Sri Lanka. The Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu has announced a relief fund of 5 billion rupees while rescue, relief, and repair works are underway with the help of the National Disaster Response Force and the army.

A McGill's 904 bus experienced a fire outside Largs on the A760 Kilbirnie Road, but the driver managed to ensure the safety of all passengers, who were uninjured. The incident caused a temporary road closure, which was later re-opened after the burnt-out bus was removed.

Jake Ball, a 25-year-old cricket bowler, is leading Nottinghamshire's bowling attack in the County Championship 2016 with six wickets in each of their first two games, including an impressive display alongside Stuart Broad, and has been praised by the team's director and coach for his exceptional form this season. However, despite his efforts, Nottinghamshire suffered an eight-wicket defeat in their second game against Lancashire.

The article describes the unveiling of a memorial stone, made from Jersey granite and dedicated to 120 men from Jersey known as "the Jersey Pals," who died in the Battle of the Somme during World War I. Part of the stone has been removed to create a heart-shaped hole and will be returned to Jersey to be included in a monument in Royal Square. The memorial was officially unveiled by Bailiff William Bailhache and was attended by a delegation from Jersey, including the Lieutenant Governor, Chief Minister, and Dean of Jersey. The memorial aims to serve as a permanent reminder of the role Jersey played in the war.

Actor John Boyega, who played Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens and was formerly part of Theatre Peckham, expressed his gratitude to the theater and stated that he aims to give back as a graduate. The theater's founder believes Boyega will inspire young members.

Thai golfer Aphibarnrat takes a one-shot lead in a European Tour event, with Fitzpatrick matching him shortly after; Luke Donald, Lee Westwood, and several others trail close behind, while Bradley Dredge withdraws due to illness.

Middlesex lost their openers early but a 279-run third-wicket stand between Ashton Agar's replacement Voges and Malan, with Malan scoring 147, has left them in a strong position to potentially claim their first win in the County Championship this season, finishing the day on 342-3, having drawn all six of their games so far. Voges scored his first ton of the season, taking him over 13,000 first-class runs in his career.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is critically injured after an incident on Penilee Road, with police locating a 54-year-old man of interest in the Dumfries and Galloway area and investigations ongoing at the scene.

The three-bedroom red brick terrace house at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, where a young John Lennon lived from 1940 to 1945, was bought by an anonymous telephone bidder in a bidding war for an undisclosed amount, having been valued between £150,000 and £250,000, located close to the famous Beatles' song location, Penny Lane.

David Ellam, a 52-year-old man from Sheepridge, Huddersfield, died after being attacked by a dog last August. The suspected owner, Aaron Joseph, 29, pleaded guilty to possessing cannabis, but denied charges related to the dog attack. A trial date has been set for February, with hopes of an earlier date, and Joseph was released on bail. The attack occurred near Riddings Road.
A body believed to be 22-year-old Thomas Bebbington from Shrewsbury was found about 10 miles away from where he was last seen entering the river near Dana Steps on November 10th.

As of January 2016, five-week-old orphaned otters are receiving daily feedings and are expected to transition to a larger outdoor enclosure with a pool by summer, where they will consume live food and potentially learn the necessary skills to survive on their own.

A 33-year-old mother of four, Joanne Thompson, was found dead at her Old Mill Court home in Newtownards, and police are investigating, seeking witnesses to a bonfire disturbance at Dakota Avenue on Monday and any activity around her home on Tuesday night and early Wednesday morning.

A record-breaking 2,270 black-tailed godwits visited Tiree, Scotland, during spring 2023, with most gathered in a small field in Kilmoluaig. Their migration to Iceland included sightings of birds tagged in France, Portugal, and Spain. The high count was attributed to favorable conditions in the Hebrides as a refueling stopover.

Rangers coach Jim Durrant, who previously worked with the first team during multiple tenures of Walter Smith and Ally McCoist, finds himself without a position in the upcoming season as manager Mark Warburton revises his coaching personnel.
A rare albino deer is drawing attention as visitors observe its adaptation processes in its new environment.

A 16-year-old named Asad Khan from Bradford passed away three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heath School, with his family alleging he had been bullied. In his final days, he shared feelings of "unsafe" in school and the belief life was "hard" with a peer. The coroner will consider whether this witness should testify at the upcoming inquest.

A 350-year-old painting depicting the 1654 coronation ceremony, found in Rokeby Park, England since 1880, has been damaged and is currently being restored. Experts have yet to identify who painted it, determine its worth, or trace its origins, though it is considered uniquely valuable as the only painted representation of the coronation.

In the football match between Macclesfield Town and Wrexham, Danny Rowe and Mitch Hancox scored for Macclesfield, making it 2-0. Danny Whittaker made it 3-0 for Macclesfield, while Jordan White missed a late penalty for Wrexham. Macclesfield moves up to 7th in the table, while Wrexham remains 15th.

A new sponsorship deal between African football's governance body, CAF, and French oil and gas company Total has been announced, with Total taking over as headline sponsor for 10 competitions, starting from the 2017 Africa cup of Nations finals, but the deal value has not been disclosed yet.

Spain's new coach Lopetegui calls up experienced players Diego Costa and Juan Mata, while Iker Casillas is overlooked, as Spain, under Lopetegui, prepare to face Belgium and Liechtenstein in their first World Cup qualifier matches, with a squad including David de Gea, Sergio Ramos, Sergio Busquets, David Silva, and Diego Costa, among others.

A deliberate wildfire, spanning over 5 kilometers and crossing a border, is currently out of control in the region, with 435 such incidents reported since May. Authorities believe that individuals in the area are intentionally starting fires, posing a risk to people's lives and properties.

Irish cricketer Boyd Rankin, who played for England from 2013-2014, has returned to play for Ireland following a period of inactivity and lack of opportunities, aiming to contribute to Ireland's qualification for Test status and the upcoming World Twenty20 tournament.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, a collaborative effort between the Patient Client Council and various stakeholders, aims to provide an independent platform for individuals affected by rare diseases, focusing on education, special services, and advocacy to improve their treatment and care.

Gloucester Cathedral aims to break traditional gender boundaries by introducing girl choristers to its choir, aiming to discover and nurture female talent, starting with auditions in April and regular performances from October.

Pedro, Chelsea's winger, suffered an injury during a game in Beijing and was hospitalized overnight with concussion. He is expected to wear a protective mask upon return to training and the rest of the squad has moved to Singapore for upcoming matches against Bayern Munich and Inter Milan.

James Taylor, a former professional cricket player who retired due to a heart condition in 2016, has joined Nottinghamshire's coaching staff to work with their academy and provide one-day cricket advice, while David Sales, a former Northamptonshire captain with over 22,000 runs, will work with their batsmen on technical aspects.

A man was charged with multiple offenses, including assault on police, in an incident witnessed by passers-by, including children, on Whiterock Road at 15:00 GMT on Friday afternoon, and he is scheduled to appear in Belfast Magistrates Court on 5 December.

On Thursday evening, the Larne RNLI's volunteer crew launched two lifeboats to tow a yacht over a mile north-east of Muck Island, after its engine failed. Despite good weather conditions, the crew successfully managed to tow the yacht to Carrick Marina, demonstrating the effective collaboration of both the inshore and all-weather lifeboats.

In an intense match, Ipswich took the lead twice through David McGoldrick and Brett Pitman, but were equalized by Kieran Revell's two goals, with the final score secured by Lee Varney, as both managers reflect on their teams' performances and future plans for the upcoming season.

A motorist from Darlington faces charges of dangerous driving, causing serious injury, and criminal damage after a bridge he was allegedly driving under collapsed on a London-bound carriageway near Maidstone, injuring a motorcyclist and causing road closures on the M25 and M26, with the incident occurring between junctions four and three and the debris being cleared over a span of two weekends.

In Platja d'Aro, holidaymakers panicked and stampeded thinking shots were fired and selfie sticks were weapons during a misguided flashmob simulating a celebrity chase, resulting in injuries and hospitalizations. The perpetrators, young women from Germany, were later released on public order charges.

A two-and-a-half-year-old boy named Jeremiah Regis, who was found dead with over 100 injuries, including a bite to the chest, at an address in Wolverhampton, has led to the murder charges against Sindyann Regis, 25, and Chevaze Mcgregor, 27. The case has been set for trial in April.

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common in Devon has led to injuries and evacuations, with firefighters battling the blaze amid high winds and a lack of water supplies, and being assisted by a police helicopter. The fire is ongoing, with crews expected to remain at the scene overnight and into early Monday.

The British Speedway Promoters' Association has reached an agreement to save a speedway club, with a 15-year lease signed for its Beaumont Park venue. Further meetings will be held to establish the club's management structure, schedule a racenight for the 2017 season, and make other necessary arrangements.

Charles Gordon, 51, has been charged with murder in the death of his sister Elizabeth Bowe, 50, who was found injured at her home in St Andrews on 17 September. The investigation into the initial police response leading up to the incident has been ordered by the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service, with a focus on the Police Investigations and Review Commissioner's (PIRC) findings, which will be submitted to the COPFS in due course.

A 29-year-old footballer, previously on loan at Ross County, has signed a permanent two-year contract with the Dingwall side, aiming to mentor younger players and contribute to the team's success, pending international clearance before his potential debut in the upcoming Scottish League Cup encounter.

In Division Two's match between Northants and Durham, Northants capitalized on Durham's fragile batting, dismissing key players for low scores, and ended the day 59-3, 107 runs behind despite losing early wickets. Max Holden (19 not out) and Chesney Hughes (16 not out) prevented further damage, while Durham succumbed to Northants' seam attack after a recent loss to Glamorgan.

A New Zealand golfer, one shot off the lead, trails joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim following the second round of the Sahalee Country Club tournament. Henderson gave away a shot at the 18th to lose the outright lead, while Lee carded a 69, and only five players are under par at the mid-point of the tournament, including Henderson, Ko, Piller, Lincicome, and Matthew who shot the lowest round of the day at one under.

Steve Watson, 56, returns to the Scotland coaching staff as assistant to manager Gordon Strachan, revisiting a role he previously held during the Euro 2008 qualifying campaign under Alex McLeish, having played alongside Strachan and Mark McGhee at Aberdeen in the 1970s and 80s.

In the ice hockey match, the Belfast Giants took an early lead over the Braehead Clan but went on to lose due to multiple goals from Ryan Martinelli, Mark Garside, Alex Foster, and Steve Saviano, leaving the final score at 5-2. The Giants have a game in hand on the Devils, who currently lead in the standings, with the teams set to compete against each other in the coming weeks.

Defending champion Jordan Spieth suffered a dramatic collapse on the final day of the 2016 Masters, losing a five-shot lead in a astonishing span of ten minutes, allowing Danny Willett to become the first Englishman since Nick Faldo in 1996 to win the event, with Faldo indicating that this devastating experience will significantly impact Spieth in future tournaments.

The article invites readers to share their recent photographs of England, providing methods such as email, Facebook, Twitter, or Instagram, and stating conditions like granting a royalty-free license for publication, while ensuring copyright ownership remains with the contributor. Safety guidelines are also emphasized.

A court heard that eye specialist Honey Rose is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter for allegedly failing to detect swollen optic discs in a patient, Vincent Barker, during a routine eye test, leading to his death due to a build-up of fluid in his brain.

Food price inflation increased in June to 4.9% compared to May's 3.2%, driven by rising pork prices, surpassing analysts' expectations but remaining below the government's target of 3.5%. This development lessens the likelihood of interest rate cuts in 2013 due to economic uncertainty, and experts anticipate China's monetary policy to stay neutral. The economy is projected to grow by 7.5% this year, which would be its slowest rate in 23 years, and Q2 GDP data will be released on 15 July.

Ivorian footballer Cheick Tiote, 30, passed away following a collapse during training with Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on 5 June. His memorial was attended by friends, family, and former team-mates, including former Newcastle United striker Papiss Cisse, who described Tiote as a brother and shared memories from their time together at the club. Tiote played seven years at Newcastle United, making over 150 appearances for the team.

Young rider Yates dropped out of the race with 75km to go on the fifth stage, allowing Sagan to claim his second victory. Pinot moved into second place overall behind leader Quintana, with Thomas advancing to sixth overall for Team Sky ahead of two remaining stages.

Fracking plans for Cuadrilla's Preston New Road site at Little Plumpton were approved in October 2020, with plans to prioritize creating jobs, investment, and community initiatives for Lancashire. Opponents have filed a legal challenge to the decision, which is ongoing.

Three 17 and 19-year-old males from north-west London, feared to be planning a trip to Syria, were arrested in Turkey upon their return to the UK, then released without charge after inquiries; this comes weeks after three schoolgirls from east London, also suspected of planning to join Islamic State in Syria, disappeared in a similar manner.

Dr. Christopher Davies, a respiratory consultant at the Royal Berkshire Hospital, expressed disappointment over the hospital's spending after a matron purchased a blackout blind for £22.95 from Homebase, which he considered overpriced, while managing staff installed it for free. The hospital's management reportedly rejected the quote for the blind, stating it was in line with NHS requirements and citing fire and infection control regulations. NHS England has since expressed interest in investigating the situation.

Adam King of Swansea's development squad contributed to a 2-0 victory over Reading, the team clinched the league title with a draw against Wolverhampton, and celebrated 31 overall wins in the 2016-17 season, following Swansea's senior team's survival in the Premier League after Crystal Palace defeated Hull 4-0, relegating Hull.

The article discusses the natural re-establishment of dunes at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, following severe December 2013 storms, and the Denbighshire council's consideration of creating a secondary dune system to bolster defense against potential future floods, due to the narrowness of the existing dunes being a cause for concern. This decision follows discussions with Natural Resources Wales, aiming to reduce the risk of a breach at this location. The coastal towns experienced significant flooding, with hundreds of properties in Rhyl, Denbighshire losing power.

The FA Cup preliminary round game between South Shields (8th tier) and Bridlington Town (9th tier) will be streamed live on various BBC digital platforms, with commentary by Conor McNamara and Danny Webber. #bbcfacup will allow viewers to interact with the commentary team. South Shields, captained by Julio Arca, are Wembley winners from last season's FA Vase final.

A 38-year-old man sustained serious, non-life-threatening facial injuries in an unexplained, possibly targeted attack on Craigmillar Castle Road, and Police Scotland is seeking witnesses and information about suspicious vehicles or behavior in the area.

A 51-year-old woman, Pamela McLaggan, has admitted to manslaughter of Jonathan Baines, 44, also known as "Willy," following an incident in Gainsborough, Lincolnshire, and has been remanded in custody ahead of sentencing in December.

A 15-year-old boy was physically attacked by a man and woman in their 40s at Patterton station, suffering facial injuries, including an eye injury, and losing his mobile phone. The incident occurred around 11:30 PM on October 3, while the boy was on a train with friends. Witnesses who were on the same train and witnessed the altercation before the attack or remained on until the train reached Neilston at 11:40 PM are urged to contact British Transport Police.

A 17-year-old from Dewsbury was questioned for suspected terrorism activities in April, and two other 17-year-olds, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, are believed to have traveled to Syria to join Islamic State. Their disappearance elicited concern from their families, who described them as "ordinary Yorkshire lads." Notably, Hassan's older brother, Hammaad Munshi, was previously arrested and convicted under the Terrorism Act at the age of 16 due to a guide to making napalm found on his computer. The authorities are investigating the recent cases.

GB's Olympic qualifying squad, featuring returnees Boxill, Peacock, Shields, and Murphy, includes 17 players who won silver in 2015, with the squad aiming to advance to final qualifying for the 2018 Winter Games in PyeongChang. Simultaneously, Italian Serie A side Cortina will play two games against the Belfast Giants in the 'Olympic Series.' These matches mark the first-ever meeting between the teams.

Matthew Perry, known for his role in Friends, is rumored to contribute to a tribute for the show's creator, James Burrows, although it is not the long-anticipated Friends reunion. The special, set to air on NBC on 21 February, will feature the original cast members. Meanwhile, Perry is set to perform in a play titled "The End of Longing" in London's West End from 2 February to 14 May.

Jones, a veteran footballer with a varied career that includes stints at Manchester United, Preston, Derby, Blackburn, Wolves, Oldham, and Wigan, made 41 appearances for Burnley last season to help them clinch the Championship title, and he started in their Premier League loss against Swansea.

A well-known Italian-Australian lawyer, Joe Acquaro, was shot dead in Melbourne, potentially due to underworld tensions that were believed to persist despite the end of a violent gangland feud in the city over a decade ago.

Air France flight 777-200 from Paris to Vancouver was diverted to Prestwick, Scotland on July 15, 2017, due to a slight smell of burning on board, prompting a normal landing, and a second aircraft was subsequently sent to return the passengers to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

A severe weather warning for strong winds and heavy rain has been issued for coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales, including Aberporth, Aberystwyth, and Anglesey, as the remains of Hurricane Gonzalo reach Britain, potentially disrupting travel and increasing the risk of surface water affecting roads.

The article details concerns about overcrowding in hospitals and prolonged wait times to see doctors, as seen through the experiences of various children, including Lily and Jake, who needed medical attention at a children's hospital in Sheffield.

A 64-year-old man, Kenneth David Dickie, died from a serious head injury at a site in Poole, where a 34-year-old man was charged with causing grievous bodily harm, and a 57-year-old woman was arrested for aiding in the cover-up and intent to cause grievous bodily harm, with both cases ongoing.

Former Manchester United forward Federico Macheda will remain at Nottingham Forest until the end of the season, but the club's attempts to sign midfielder Andre Moritz have been unsuccessful due to contractual complications.

The body of Christopher Huxtable, 34, who had been missing since February's building collapse in Swansea, was found and recovered with a guard of honor; however, two other men, Ken Cresswell, 57, and John Shaw, 61, remain missing. MP Carolyn Harris expressed condolences for the family, yet emphasized concerns for the families of the missing men, whose whereabouts remain unresolved.

The Bosnia-Herzegovina international is aiming for match fitness after a hernia injury but is doubtful for the game against QPR, while QPR is missing Jordan Cousins due to a quadricep injury and has Kazenga LuaLua back in training but his availability is uncertain. Bristol City coach Lee Johnson is focusing on a crucial match against QPR, aiming to close the gap with competing teams in the standings.

Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano, chosen by ESA in 2009, expressed immense joy during his 2013 mission to the International Space Station, where he conducted two spacewalks, orbiting Earth over 2,656 times while traveling over 110 million km.

A 16-year-old England Knights player, Joe Arundel, who made 44 appearances for his previous team, is joining Hull FC, expressing excitement and some nervousness about the new challenge and the pressure of joining a big club known for building a winning mentality and a focus on the future.

Ulster Bank is working to rectify a payment issue affecting approximately 600,000 customers, with the goal of resolving it by Saturday, reassuring customers they will not be out of pocket. This is the second such incident for RBS, NatWest, and Ulster Bank since a 2012 IT meltdown, but the banking group has since significantly upgraded its computer systems.

Tanzania led Kenya 2-1 in the 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, with goals from Omari Mwanahamisi and an unspecified second scorer for Tanzania, while Christine Nafula scored for Kenya, but they were unable to secure an equaliser. Meanwhile, in the third-place play-off, Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1.
McDonald's in Japan is rationing French fries due to a shortage caused by industrial action affecting American potato suppliers, and they are importing additional supplies to meet demand.

The addition of Permian and Khalidi increases the total purse for the June 3 Classic to £1.625m, with Cracksman, who beat Permian in the Derby Trial, being the favorite. Meanwhile, 1,000-1 outsider Diore Lia, trained by John Jenkins and ridden by apprentice Gina Mangan, will be participating to generate publicity and funds for Great Ormond Street Children's Hospital.

Antonio Griezmann, Atletico Madrid's leading scorer in La Liga, has a haematoma on his left foot but no bone injury, causing him to miss France's game against Ivory Coast on Tuesday while he undergoes treatment in Madrid, with Atletico facing league leaders Real Madrid at the Vicente Calderon after 11 games.

Australian prop forward Willie Mason, a veteran with a 15-year career in the NRL and 24 tests for the Kangaroos, has joined the Super League's Catalans Dragons, aiming to bolster their struggling team after two losses this season.

A recent survey reports a significant 11% rise in dog feces on UK beaches, with a striking 71% increase in Scotland. The Marine Conservation Society praises pet owners for using bags to clean up after their dogs, but urges them to properly dispose of the waste in provided dog bins, rather than leaving it on the beach. Despite the rise in dog mess, overall litter levels decreased this year.

The article summarizes that the UK government's introduction of court fees in 2013, aiming to decrease malicious and weak cases, resulted in a 79% reduction over three years. However, trade unions like Unison argued these fees prevented workers from accessing justice, and the Supreme Court agreed, ruling the government acted unlawfully and unconstitutionally. The fees were found to be indirectly discriminatory towards women, as they make up a higher proportion of discrimination case claimants, with fees ranging between £390 and £1,200 for a hearing. The Supreme Court's ruling was deemed a "tremendous victory" for employment rights in the country.

In the football match between Dagenham & Redbridge and Wycombe Wanderers, Wycombe won 3-2 despite having Garry Thompson and Josh Passley dismissed. Dagenham, who drew level through Luke Guttridge, remain in the relegation zone, while Wycombe moved up to 6th position. Manager John Still believes the team's quality and resilience will help them climb the table.

Bee-eaters, native to southern Europe, have nested in Britain for a second consecutive year, eliciting delight from the RSPB, as they burrowed tunnels in a Low Gelt Quarry and attracted over 1,000 visitors to the nearby RSPB viewpoint within two weeks.

According to police, a boy witnessed his father's boat capsize on the River Wey in Guildford at approximately 13:10 BST on Monday. The boy attempted to save his father but was advised against it by onlookers. Divers are searching the river at Millmead and the public has been asked not to enter the water if they spot the missing kayaker, instead contacting 999 immediately. The river has a flood warning due to heavy rain over the weekend, is a popular spot for kayakers, and the Wey Valley Kayak Club had warned earlier on Monday that the section from Godalming Wharf to Thames Lock was not safe.

A stone thrown by a captive elephant at Rabat Zoo in Morocco fatally injured a child, according to a zoo statement, with the elephant's behavior considered unusual and likely driven by boredom or frustration; the incident comes following three similar but rare incidents in US zoos, as reported by the zoo's statement.

MP for North West Durham, Ms Glass, has joined the shadow cabinet amidst a wave of Labour resignations calling for leadership change, with her predecessor, Ms Powell, stating that party leader Mr Corbyn's position has become "untenable" due to his failure to provide effective opposition.

Chelsea lead the Premier League with 59 points, five points separating them from second-placed Tottenham to sixth-placed Manchester United, with Manchester City, Arsenal, Liverpool, and United considered strong title contenders. Manager Conte emphasizes the importance of focus and concentration for the remaining 14 games, including a challenging match against Burnley, who have won seven consecutive home games. Conte also notes that teams at the bottom can pose a threat to the top four and six teams are in the title race.

A dispersal order has been issued in Llangefni, allowing police to remove troublemakers and underage individuals from the area, aiming to prevent anti-social behavior, reduce criminal damage, and protect young people from the adverse effects of alcohol.

Dutch international midfielder Georginio de Roon played 33 games and scored five goals for Middlesbrough in the Premier League before the 2016-17 season, and manager Garry Monk has expressed interest in signing Chelsea's Lewis Baker.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, celebrating humor in children's literature, will be relaunched in 2016 during the author's centenary celebrations, with a focus on making it even more impactful and ensuring a robust future for this unique award.

White supremacist Frazier Glenn Miller Jr, known as Frazier Glenn Cross, received a death sentence for capital murder, attempted murder, and weapons charges after he targeted sites in Kansas, stating he was motivated by anti-Semitic beliefs. He shouted "heil Hitler" upon sentencing and indicated he was indifferent to the outcome.

The city council plans to introduce a larger self-service bike scheme from April 2017, modeled after London's 'Boris bikes,' with bikes strategically placed at accessible locations such as district centers, universities, and public transport facilities, expecting to be funded through sponsorship income without affecting taxpayers.

Senegal international Sakho, 27, is working his way back to fitness after undergoing back surgery and three months of rehab, following which he will need several weeks of pre-season training before he can be considered for selection in the Premier League.

Prices in Northern Ireland's residential property market experienced a slight 0.8% increase in the third quarter of 2021, compared to a 5.4% rise compared to the same quarter in 2015, with the Antrim and Newtownabbey district recording the highest annual increase (7.3%) and apartments showing the lowest annual rise (4%).

The delivery of huge wind turbine parts on rural roads in Dumfries and Galloway was highlighted, with one successful passage over Bargrennan Bridge and another resulting in an accident with the lorry and cargo ending up in a ditch on the A713.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is considering temporarily downsizing maternity services at Glan Clwyd Hospital due to a staffing shortage, but the suggestion faces opposition from locals who fear travel implications, with public meetings set for September to discuss varying options including maintaining all services.

Mignon du Preez scored a century for South Africa in an ODI match, helping her team to 272-6. Ireland struggled in response, being bowled out for 204 by South African seamer Masabata Klaas, with du Preez leading a recovery from a middle-order wobble for the Proteas.

British high jumper Holly Peake, aged 30, is setting her sights on breaking the Welsh record for high jump at Cardiff International Sports Stadium as she aims to qualify for Team GB in the Rio Olympics, having already achieved a personal best of 4.40m, with the official qualification standard set at 4.50m by British Athletics.
Firefighters battled a 10-hour blaze at a building site in Llanwern caused by a deliberate setting, involving a large amount of scrapped railway sleepers, with local police investigating.

A charity event organized by the Nepal Scotland Association, Mercy Corps, and the city council, featuring a Singing Bowl Concert at St Giles' Cathedral, took place to raise money for the victims of the recent devastating earthquake in Nepal, many of whom are members of the Association.

UEFA imposed a suspension on Neil Lennon, Hibs head coach, for acts of violence against the referee during a Europa League match, resulting in his dismissal and an automatic ban for the return leg. Hibs appealed the suspension after losing to Brondby on penalties in the tie.

A fire occurred 1,100m beneath the sea bed at the ICL UK Boulby mine, causing 7 workers to be hospitalized for smoke inhalation, with 11 initially unaccounted for. Polystyrene blocks are believed to have ignited, and the Health and Safety Executive has served an improvement notice on the company, giving them until June 27 to comply. The investigation into the incident is ongoing.

Two British and French tourists were caught naked at the Unesco World Heritage site, Machu Picchu, and questioned for offences against morality; the local authorities are in contact with the British Foreign Office, and no arrests or charges have been made.

Ivan Rakitic, a 28-year-old Croatia international, is expected to re-sign with Barcelona for £109m ($125m euros) on Friday, prolonging his successful tenure with the team, having already made 145 appearances since his 2014 transfer from Sevilla.

A couple from Halstead suffered life-altering injuries in a two-hour torture incident on April 26, with one perpetrator described as a black man in his 20s, 5ft 10in tall, and police continue investigating the "shocking crime."

The Wickerman Festival, scheduled for 25 and 26 July at East Kirkcarswell Farm near Dundrennan, Scotland, announced Dizzee Rascal as its opening night headliner; a diverse lineup featuring Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, The Zombies, Big Country, The Feeling, and additional acts will be announced in the coming weeks, offering a mix of hip hop, pop, folk, Motown, and alternative rock.

English rugby players Foden (Saints) and Brown (Quins), both 26, are performing well in the Aviva Premiership, with Foden scoring his third try in two matches and Saints beating Quins 24-3. Both are aiming to be included in the upcoming England Six Nations squad, with Brown set to return after 12 years, while Foden hopes to help more Saints players join England for the tournament.

In Dagenham, a motorcyclist aged 22 died after colliding with a Vauxhall Zafira, and the rear passenger, aged 10, is in a serious condition. The car driver, aged 38, was not injured. Police are investigating the crash, appealing for witnesses, and have not made any arrests.

Pfizer has agreed to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, whose flagship product crisaborole (a cream for eczema) is awaiting US FDA approval, aiming to address a significant unmet medical need for a large eczema patient population in the US; according to Pfizer, crisaborole could generate $2bn annually if approved, with 18-25 million US eczema sufferers and few safe, appropriate treatments currently available.

A street fight on Oxlow Lane, Dagenham, resulted in the recovery of multiple weapons and the arrest of two teenage boys, with no reported injuries, according to authorities who stated that the seizure of the weapons may have prevented further harm.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault following an early morning attack on a 19-year-old woman in Gorsedd Gardens near Cardiff Civic Centre.

Scottish Conservative MSP John Lamont resigned from the Ettrick, Roxburgh, and Berwickshire constituency seat to contest as a candidate in the Westminster by-election, aiming to defeat SNP's Calum Kerr, with the Lib Dems nominating Catriona Bhatia as their candidate.

The EU, including major producers France and Germany, can now export beef to Canada following Canada's recognition of the EU's successful measures in eradicating BSE and a growing trend in global trade, especially after a Russian import ban and weaker Chinese demand impacted European farm exports, leading to an EU aid package and a resumption of beef imports from the US under strict monitoring.

The European Commission plans to sanction nations on a forthcoming tax blacklist for non-cooperation, aims to create a unified list of non-cooperative jurisdictions, and intends to intensify investigations into banks and tax advisers aiding offshore tax evasion, following the Panama Papers leak revealing secretive practices of wealthy individuals and businesses using tax havens.

Archaeologists unearthed Bronze Age burnt mounds, remains of pottery, and fragments of kilns for drying grain at Torvean, some of which were linked to heating systems for cooking, washing wool, or small saunas, during the construction of a new road easing traffic flow through Inverness.

Oldham secured a important victory over Southend, with Main scoring the winning goal after Forte's assist, increasing their lead above the League One relegation zone, while Southend remain in 13th place.

Actor and Irish language advocate, Lally, renowned for roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, Alexander, and The Secret of Kells, passed away peacefully following a short illness, leaving behind his wife Peggy and their children, Saileog, Darach, and Maghnus.

The Derby City Council, facing a need to save £79m over three years, initially wanted to close Moorways Pool to save £350,000 a year. However, after identifying savings in back-office areas and management restructuring, they committed to keep it open for a year. The pool, which is 33m long, is in need of repair, and its closure would have left only one other public pool in the city, potentially affecting swimming lessons for 1,200 young people weekly, as noted by the Derbyshire Amateur Swimming Association.

Children previously held captive in Boko Haram-controlled areas were detained in a military barracks in Maiduguri, according to a UN spokesman, with human rights groups voicing concerns over a lack of proper legal process for these detentions and questioning the prolonged detention of these children as part of the counter-insurgency operations in north-eastern Nigeria.

Alexander suffered a broken cheekbone in a victory against Rangers, while Gallacher is a doubt for the Edinburgh derby due to an ankle injury, and Hearts are considering a goalkeeping signing, Lee Hollis, as a possible replacement for Neil after his injury.

Basketball player Chelsey Lee, 26, who played for Bucheon KEB Hana Bank in the Women's Korean Basketball League (WKBL), is under investigation for allegedly falsifying her and her father's birth certificates to show a South Korean grandmother, which allowed her to play as a foreign player. The WKBL has announced her suspension for life and annulment of her records, and will eliminate the extra quota for international players with Korean ancestry following this incident.

The article discusses the release of an app that analyzes wireless signals to optimize wifi speed, suggesting many homes and offices worldwide are underperforming. It further explains findings from a 2015 report by Ofcom stating that despite improvements in super-fast broadband availability and usage, 8% of UK homes still can't access speeds above 10Mbps, and small businesses are poorly served in this regard.

Manchester United player Paul Pogba used social media to address his performance in the team's 1-1 draw with Liverpool, and consensus top scorer Zlatan Ibrahimovic, feeling the weight of pressure, expressed his preference for team success over personal accolades and an impressive 14th Premier League goal.

A large metal object discovered in a river in Salinopolis, Brazil, is confirmed to be debris from Europe's Alphasat satellite, launched from the Kourou base in French Guiana last July. Brazilian authorities have contacted the UK Space Agency to arrange for its removal, as the object is non-radioactive and the size of a car.

The article discusses James Purnell's warning that decriminalizing non-payment of the BBC TV license could lead to a £200m loss for the BBC, potentially forcing the closure of BBC Four, CBBC, and CBeebies, and increasing the license fee due to higher evasion rates. The issue of decriminalization will not be discussed until charter renewal talks in 2017. Additionally, Labour MP John McDonnell has called for the BBC to reverse its decision to close BBC Three and receive a license fee increase tracked by inflation during the charter renewal in 2017.

Derry suffered their first defeat of the season, losing 2-1 to Harps, with key moments including a David Scully goal on the stroke of half-time and a Ryan Curran strike mid-way through the second half, while former Derry player Ryan Curran scored Harps' second goal.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has stated that securities offered through Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), using blockchain or distributed ledger technology, must be registered, following concerns over an investment bubble and lack of investor protection. The SEC clarified that existing securities regulations, rather than crypto-currency specific laws, apply to ICOs.

Operation Anagram, initiated by Strathclyde Police in 2006 after the murder of Angelika Kluk, has helped convict Peter Tobin of the murders of Dinah McNicol and Vicky Hamilton. The operation, while being scaled back, will never end, and anyone with information regarding Tobin can still contact the Anagram incident room. Det Sup David Swindle, who formed the operation, is proud of the success in bringing closure to some bereaved families, and the search for truth about what Tobin has done will continue. Tobin is currently serving three life sentences for the murders of Vicky Hamilton, Dinah McNicol, and Angelika Kluk.

In the Australian Grand Prix, Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel emerged victorious over Lewis Hamilton, with Hamilton acknowledging Ferrari performed better overall, yet expressing optimism for future races, particularly the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. Vettel admitted it is challenging to beat Mercedes, but Ferrari aims to maintain their strong performance in future races.

The Southwark Crown Court is hearing a trial where Mr Clifford, a former celebrity lawyer, is accused of indecent assault in the 1980s. The alleged victim claims he exposed himself, forced her to perform a sex act, and threatened to rape or kill her. Mr Clifford denies the allegation and the case is adjourned until Monday for his testimony. During his police interview, he gave a "no comment" response when asked about the allegation, and previously stated he never coerced anyone into sexual activity. Notable clients represented by Mr Clifford include Simon Cowell, Jade Goody, and Muhammad Ali.

In the given article, Coach Steve Tandy anticipates a physical and intense match between Ospreys and Scarlets in the Pro12, despite both teams enduring contrasting results in their recent games (one being high-scoring, the other being try-less). The match is crucial for Ospreys in closing the gap between their performance and that of Scarlets. However, the participation of Nicky Smith and the fitness of Brendon Leonard is uncertain due to injury.

The annual Diwali celebration on Belgrave Road (Golden Mile), Leicester, was marked by massive crowds, a large firework display, and an array of cultural events, and is considered one of the largest Diwali parties outside India. The festival, which celebrates light over darkness and is observed by Hindus, Sikhs, and Jains, is open to all, reflecting the city's inclusivity, and features various forms of entertainment and art.

Rosie Ross's charity, Rosie's Helping Hands, raised  £350,000 for young people in Aldridge over the past 16 years, but will be winding down after the final annual Rosie's Walk on Aldridge Airfield on Sunday, as her parents, Karen and Mark, feel the charity should not continue past the same amount of time they had with their daughter. The charity has funded projects such as a pirate-themed play area on the children's ward at Walsall Manor Hospital, greatly improving the area and providing a source of normalizing play for sick children.

Macmillan Cancer Support, partnering with Cwm Taf Health Board, seeks planning permission for a £5m investment to build a new palliative care unit at the Llantrisant site in Wales. The unit will offer inpatient, outpatient, and day services for patients with incurable cancer and other conditions, and will be Macmillan's largest single investment in Wales. The proposed unit aims to improve care for patients through a comfortable environment, better access to specialist tests and treatment, and the inclusion of kitchen and communal areas. Construction may begin later this year, with an anticipated opening in late 2018 or early 2019.

Northern Wales is recognized as one of the top 10 travel destinations in the world, featuring attractions like Surf Snowdonia, Zipworld's zip lines, and the extensive Snowdonia National Park. The Welsh government welcomed the news and stated that the increase in tourists contributed to the economy for 2017. The destinations, highlighted by Lonely Planet, included Choquequirao in Peru, Taranaki in New Zealand, the Azores in Portugal, Northern Wales, De Australia, Aysén in Chile, the Tuamotus in French Polynesia, the Georgia Coast in the United States, Perak in Malaysia, and the Skellig Ring in Ireland.

The Church of England and the Church of Scotland, through the Columba Declaration, have committed to strengthening their partnership and growing in communion, with a focus on recognizing each other formally and welcoming clergy and lay people migrating across borders, while respecting their separate constitutional responsibilities within the UK.

The article describes L/Bdr Parkinson, a wounded Afghanistan war veteran who carried the Olympic torch, receiving an overwhelming number of friend requests on Facebook as a result, with the platform advising him to switch to a page or consider the subscribe feature since he has become a public figure due to his status as a public figure, as evidenced by the massive amount of support and requests.

A large seizure of Captagon pills, a widely consumed synthetic stimulant in the Middle East, was found at Beirut's airport, leading to the detention of five individuals, including a reported Saudi prince, as they prepared to board a private jet bound for Saudi Arabia, marking the largest such drug smuggling operation at the airport to date.

A police inquiry is underway regarding allegations within Kids Company, a charity providing support to vulnerable inner-city children, run by Camila Batmanghelidjh. The charity has asserted its focus on safety and security of the children it serves while assuring robust policies and procedures to prevent misconduct. The investigating team can be contacted via 0208 217 6538, and concerned individuals can contact the National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children via 0808 800 5000.

The Queen, who celebrates her 90th birthday this week, is renowned for her ability to mimic the local brogue of Norfolk and, according to her cousin Margaret Rhodes, possesses a developed sense of humor, especially when things go awry. She can also imitate a Scottish accent due to her time at Balmoral, and on her birthday at Windsor Castle, she will unveil a plaque on the Queen's Walkway while receiving salutes and beacons from various locations across the UK.

The report by UN-Habitat states that Latin America remains the world's most urbanized region, with an average income disparity of 20:1 between its richest and poorest citizens, and suggests that the region use its current economic stability and slower population growth to address urban inequality, particularly concerning income, employment, and labor informality, with Colombia, Paraguay, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Bolivia, the Dominican Republic, Argentina, and Guatemala showing increased inequality between 1990 and 2009, but a potential positive trend with decreasing urban poverty, indigence, and unemployment according to Erik Vittrup of UN-Habitat.

A Carmarthenshire Labour councillor, Tegwen Devichand, is under investigation for sharing a far-right group's post that supports capital punishment for sex offenders. The post was initially shared by Britain First. Devichand, the Labour deputy group leader, opposes the approval of removing English-stream education at Ysgol Llangennech and has been accused of working with UKIP to undermine the council's decision. She denies any wrongdoing and claims to be facing a "hate campaign," with one Labour councillor, Kim Thomas, describing the decision as "segregation... at worst, apartheid." The Welsh Labour party has acknowledged the complaints and launched an investigation.

The Iraq War Families Campaign Group, led by Relatives of British troops killed in Iraq, launched a crowdfunding campaign to seek legal action against those responsible for the war and the deaths of their loved ones, after the Chilcot report found that the then-Prime Minister Tony Blair overstated the threat posed by Saddam Hussein and sent ill-prepared troops into battle, without making any findings on individual illegality. The campaign, which aimed to raise £50,000, has now received enough funding to pursue legal advice on potential legal actions.

Adnan Syed, who is currently serving a life sentence for the 1999 murder of Hae Min Lee, will get a new trial, as lawyers can now present new evidence, including a potential alibi and a challenge to the reliability of mobile phone records used in the original trial.

A 16-year-old boy was found guilty of assault with a machete on a taxi driver after a party in Dundee, Scotland, and another 16-year-old was charged with theft following the same incident. The assailant, who cannot be named due to legal reasons, has previous custodial sentence records for assaults at younger ages.

In a narrow victory, John Clancy, a long-time Labour councillor, became the new leader of Birmingham City Council after defeating fellow party members in a closely contested ballot. He plans to focus on housing, financial management, free school meals, and regeneration outside the city center, while addressing government concerns about the council's operations.

In the June edition of Empire magazine, actor Roger Moore discussed his early meetings with Bond director Guy Hamilton, aiming to distance his portrayal of James Bond from Sean Connery's iconic version while still maintaining the character's essence. The interview preceded the release of Skyfall, featuring Daniel Craig as 007 and directed by Sam Mendes. The film's production featured a car chase involving Aston Martin DB5s, a nod to Connery's earlier Bond films, Goldfinger, and Thunderball. The article also highlighted the contributions of unsung hero Yat Malmgren, a Swedish dance teacher who helped Connery refine his movements and gestures, and scriptwriter Terence Young, who introduced Connery to Savile Row tailors and instructed him to sleep in the suits to establish Bond's unique sense of style.

"Historic England encourages public documentation this Halloween of the ancient 'witches' marks', religious symbols believed to offer protective powers against witches and evil spirits in buildings, such as the Daisy Wheel and various Virgin Mary references, found in medieval homes, churches, and other structures throughout the UK, as knowledge about them is scarce."

The article describes a humorously contentious exchange between Prime Minister Theresa May, Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, and actor Sir Tony Robinson during Prime Minister's Questions, in which Corbyn compared May's Brexit strategy to Baldrick's inscrutable "cunning plans" from the TV show Blackadder, and Robinson agreed, while also mocking May's famous phrase "Brexit means Brexit."

The Liverpool County Court ruled against Jet2 and three other UK airlines who attempted to delay compensation payments for flight delays, stating that justice delayed is justice denied. This decision may prompt thousands of similar claims for compensation in the UK. The ruling stems from European regulations which require airlines to pay passengers compensation for flight cancellations or long delays, unless these circumstances are extraordinary.

Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan, has stated that the number of jobs moving out of the UK to EU cities like Dublin and Frankfurt is no longer in the UK's control, as the EU has the power to dictate more job relocations from London to the EU over time. French Prime Minister Edouard Philippe, at the same event, promised a pro-banker environment, offering incentives such as lower taxes, English law courts, and English-speaking schools, to attract banks to Paris. HSBC's CEO, Stuart Gulliver, has already announced plans to move up to 1,000 bankers to Paris, but expressed reservations about renewed sentiment towards bankers in France.

China has deployed surface-to-air missiles on a disputed island in the South China Sea, which is claimed by multiple countries and considered a resource-rich shipping route, causing tensions and concerns about potential militarization, with the US expecting a serious conversation with China over the issue.

Scientists found that Adanson's house spiders use their silk draglines to stabilize their bodies in mid-air and brake, allowing them to land poised to catch prey. This discovery could inspire the design of small, maneuverable robots that can adjust silk tension for improved control and stability.

The Supreme Court has ruled that the UK government is not legally obliged to consult devolved assemblies, including in Wales, on Brexit, but the Welsh Government is expecting the UK government to uphold the Sewel Convention, which grants the assembly a say, and there may be a vote in the Welsh Assembly regarding the triggering of Article 50, though it will not serve as a veto on leaving the EU.

The Co-op Bank, renowned for its ethical stance and with four million customers, is on the verge of finalizing a plan for recapitalization with existing investors, having earlier sought to sell itself due to failing to meet Bank of England regulations, while negotiations continue for the separation of its pension fund from the Co-operative Group's scheme.

The Swansea tidal lagoon project, estimated by NRW to potentially kill 21% of salmon and 25% of sea trout each year, has been disputed by Tidal Lagoon Power (TLP) who claim the figures lack a "clear scientific basis" and that their own modeling suggests a "worst case scenario" of only 2% of all fish species being affected. Both parties have expressed frustration with the other's approach to data and methodology. The UK government is currently reviewing the viability of the scheme, and the Welsh Government has given its support but is seeking clarity on the UK government's position.

The article summarizes the most memorable and questionable moments from a reality TV show competition, highlighting instances of sexism, lack of preparation, and comedic gaffes, such as a hypnotherapist advocating for outdated attire for women, a contestant designing a sexist board game, and a participant delivering a poorly prepared pitch filled with coughing fits, ultimately leading to his elimination.

The Home Affairs select committee found that the immigration cap, limiting the recruitment of skilled workers from non-EU countries, has been "counter-productive" as it has increased EU migration and potentially led to a crisis in the NHS due to the rejection of nurse visa applications, while not significantly reducing net migration.

The court cleared Aaeron Evans of manslaughter in the death of off-duty soldier Matthew Boyd, 20, who was beaten outside a bar in Brecon, Wales, by Jake Vallely. Vallely is scheduled for sentencing on December 8th, while Evans was acquitted due to being absent during the attack. The case sparked calls for non-violence during drinking sessions from Senior Investigating Officer Det Supt David Guiney. The Boyd family described the soldier as an "all-rounder" with a promising career ahead of him, and expressed their grief after the loss.

The BBC, in collaboration with tech company This Place, is trialing a brainwave-reading headset that allows users to control their iPlayer on-demand platform, potentially facilitating entertainment for people with disabilities who find traditional remote controls challenging.

The Chief Inspector of Schools, Meilyr Rowlands, and Strategic Director for Estyn, Claire Morgan, testified that the focus on certain performance indicators in schools has led to a focus on borderline grades, leaving more able learners undersupported. Ministers have agreed to take steps to address this issue and improve opportunities for all students, including implementing changes to measurement systems and supporting programs for gifted students.

"Unreleased in 1981-1984, Out Among the Stars by Johnny Cash, featuring duets with June Carter and Waylon Jennings, is set to debut in March, marking the fourth posthumous album release since his death in 2003. The album, found in a vault by John Carter Cash in 2012, comprises of recordings that were never released, and is considered a "work of art" that will appeal to fans and further bolster the Cash estate's success in music sales."

The tribunal ruled that Maria McKeith was unfairly dismissed from the Ardoyne Association due to her role as primary carer for her disabled daughter, in breach of the Disability Discrimination Act 1995. The finding was upheld in appeal court, with Ms McKeith awarded £10,000 for injury to feelings and other compensation. The Equality Commission emphasized that employers must be aware of their responsibilities to protect employees and primary carers of disabled persons from discrimination.

Scottish midfielder Shaun Malcolm Dorrans, who had spells at Livingston, West Bromwich Albion, and Norwich City, has joined Rangers after two bids from the Ibrox club were accepted by Norwich, becoming manager Pedro Caixinha's ninth summer signing. Dorrans expressed his delight at the move and shared his long-standing admiration for the club.

Scotland's teams, skipped by siblings Eve and Thomas Brewster, achieved victories in Perth's Dewars Centre, securing men's and women's spots at the European Championships. Eve, inspired by playing at home, and Thomas, supported by new coach Glenn Howard, are excited to compete in their home country with great motivation. Anna Sloan, Thomas' long-term girlfriend and third player for Team Muirhead, returns from injury this week.

Councillor Pierre Oxley accused the council of being unclear about the sand-to-shingle ratio in a beach recharge project, and called for a scrutiny meeting on Tuesday, which Peter Halliday, in response, called a form of "scaremongering". The meeting will be held to discuss resident concerns about the composition of the beach, particularly its playability, while the council argues they have been transparent throughout the process.

John Nelms, co-owner of Dundee Football Club, announced plans to submit a land use application for property in Camperdown Park, aiming to improve the club, as they grapple with financial losses, rising stadium maintenance costs, and stadium infrastructure issues.

In the Criterium du Dauphine, Spain's Jesus Herrada won stage two by breaking away during the final climb, while overall leader Alberto Contador and Chris Froome finished eight and eight places behind, with Contador retaining his lead over Froome by six seconds heading into the hilly third stage.

Ex-EastEnders star Sian Blake and her two sons, Zachary and Amon, were found dead at their home with head and neck injuries. The police are seeking her partner, Arthur Simpson-Kent, who is being investigated for the triple murder. Sian's family alleges she had expressed a desire to leave him previously. The Met has referred its handling of the case to the IPCC for investigation.

Due to ongoing rain and a backlog of matches, Wimbledon organizers have decided to play on the traditional rest day (Middle Sunday) for the fourth time in history, with play starting at 11:30 BST on all courts, including Centre and Court One, to prevent sections of the draw from getting too far apart.

Despite initially agreeing to lead Sunderland temporarily, Dick Advocaat decided to stay on and save them from relegation last season. However, he is now leaving the club after only eight games this season, having failed to secure a win, breaking the trend of managers joining to save the club from the drop and leaving in the next season.

Russia's economy, already struggling due to energy exports decline and Western sanctions, is predicted to experience a 0.8% GDP decline next year, following a 0.6% GDP growth in 2014, and the rouble has lost about half its value against the dollar in 2020, prompting the government to take measures to secure banks and stabilize the economy, such as doubling deposit guarantees and providing direct loans to major banks like Sberbank.

Kenyan opposition leader Raila Odinga has brought a case to the Supreme Court, alleging massive election fraud, after losing the presidential election to incumbent Uhuru Kenyatta, and claims to have concrete evidence of irregularities. The international community, including EU foreign affairs chief Federica Mogherini and former UN Secretary General Kofi Annan, have urged calm amid fears of violence, while Odinga insists this does not mean he is giving up the fight. The Supreme Court is anticipated to provide Odinga a second chance to demonstrate its independence, following a previous case in 2013 when he challenged the presidential results.

A 60-year-old certified diver experienced trouble while scuba diving at Agincourt Reef in Far North Queensland, resulting in his death despite CPR efforts. This incident follows two recent fatalities due to cardiac arrests among French tourists who were snorkeling on Michaelmas Cay.

The UK and Scottish governments, along with Dundee City Council, have agreed a 3.7 million pound public service obligation (PSO) contract to continue Loganair's operation of the Dundee-London Stansted route for another two years, providing two weekday return flights and one return flight on Sundays. This move aims to maintain connectivity, support trade and tourism in Scotland, and potentially attract additional routes.

WWE is set to launch its streaming service, featuring major live events and original series, in mainland China through its Chinese partner PPTV, hoping to win over audiences with localized content and potentially Chinese stars, following a similar strategy of other global sports looking to tap into China's vast population.

Three men, including a West Midlands police officer, are being questioned on suspicions of providing false information about a supposed kidnap plot involving a terrorist threat and on charges of misconduct, leading to heightened security alerts in the region last December.

Ireland secured a convincing 5-1 victory in a must-win quarter-final match against Poland, with key contributions from players like McKee, O'Donoghue, and Magee. The win guarantees Ireland a spot in the semi-final against Wales, with the victor advancing to the final and World League 3. France and Scotland will play in the other semi-final at the same venue. Ireland coach Craig Fulton was pleased with his team's performance but believes they left several more goals on the field.

A 38-year-old named Philip Craig was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 25 years, after he killed 24-year-old Christopher Laskaris, who suffered from Asperger's Syndrome and bi-polar disorder, in Leeds, in November. Craig, exploiting Laskaris' vulnerabilities, stabbed him and took various possessions, including a TV, games console, and guitars. The court stated that Craig had targeted Laskaris' vulnerability for personal gain, and Laskaris' family released a statement expressing their relief at the justice served but their ongoing pain and loss. A second man, Dempsey Pattison, had been charged with the murder but his case was discharged in February.

The Metropolitan Police has closed the reinvestigation of Kester David's 2010 death under a bridge, apologizing to his family for earlier failures and insensitivity in the initial investigation, while also acknowledging a catalogue of errors, but finding no evidence of a third party's involvement in his death.

In 2015, football had the highest overall attendance of 43.4 million, followed by three horse racing events. Rugby union attendances increased due to the Rugby World Cup, reaching 7.5 million. The top 10 individual events, excluding the World Cup, had a combined attendance of 2.5 million, with Wimbledon leading. Formula 1's British Grand Prix had the most attendances per event day. Two new events, MotoGP's British Grand Prix and Badminton Horse Trials, entered the top 10.
