Despite falling short of the 75 million in 2012 (due to the Olympics), overall attendances rose by 6% in 2015 without the one-off effects of the Olympics or the Rugby World Cup. Upcoming major events in 2016 include the UCI Track Cycling World Championships, the European Aquatics Championships, and the FIH Women's Champions Trophy in hockey.

Beyoncé topped the Forbes list for the highest-earning musician of 2013-2014, amassing $115 million, thanks to her self-titled album release, 95 shows, and endorsement deals, with Taylor Swift, Pink, Rihanna, and Katy Perry following in that order. Other high-profile artists like Madonna, Nicki Minaj, and Alicia Keys didn't make the top 10.

The Scottish National Party argues that it has more support among MPs than Labour, with 54 SNP MPs compared to 40 expressing support for Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, but Speaker John Bercow maintains that Labour remains the official opposition due to parliamentary rules, despite challenges to Corbyn's leadership.

Villagers in Crickhowell successfully launch their own bid to purchase The Corn Exchange, aiming to transform it into independent shops and flats, after Punch Taverns halted their plans following local protests.

RIT Capital officially declines to make a formal bid for Alliance Trust, ending informal merger talks, and steps out of official stock market takeover and merger procedures, while Alliance Trust continues its internal strategic review to potentially restructure, including the possibility of sale, outsourcing investment, or a deal with RIT, following activist investor-induced changes.

Alexis Scott, 39, a former Police Community Support Officer, was convicted and sentenced for six counts of theft and misfeasance for tricking passengers into believing they had too much cash on them when boarding flights at the North Terminal in April 2013. Her crime targeted long-haul passengers and involved taking around £13,500 from them, which the police later reimbursed. The judge criticized her for exploiting victims' "lack of sophistication and panic," commenting that it severely affected public trust and the international reputation of the country.

Educational platform TrueTube has received multiple Bafta award nominations, with its productions Refugee and Katie contending for best drama and learning awards respectively, while Horrible Histories' Shakespeare special has earned nominations for best comedy, writing, and best performer categories. Other double nominees include Cartoon Network's The Amazing World of Gumball, CBBC's Hetty Feather, and The Dog Ate my Homework. Various films and games, such as Zootropolis, Star Wars: The Force Awakens, and Lego Star Wars: The Force Awakens, have also been nominated in various categories.

Lady Mary Soames, the last child of Sir Winston Churchill, bequeathed most of her art collection to the National Trust, Houses of Parliament, and Churchill War Rooms. Key paintings like Coast Scene near Cannes (1935) and View From a Bathing Hut at the Miami Surf Club, 1946 will be displayed in these locations. The collection, which also includes Churchill's works and a painting of him at his easel, was accepted in lieu of inheritance tax. Culture Minister Ed Vaizey emphasized the significance of showcasing Churchill's artistic talent, as it offers an insight into his personal life beyond his political career.

An ex-ombudsman investigator is under arrest for allegedly stealing sensitive security documents, potentially putting lives at risk; the PSNI is conducting a criminal investigation, and there are calls for police to be involved earlier in such matters to ensure independence and fairness.

Phyllis Schlafly, a conservative activist who opposed feminism, Communism, and the Equal Rights Amendment, played a significant role in shaping the political landscape of the 1970s and 1980s, and was credited for creating a climate favorable to Ronald Reagan's presidency. She championed traditional family values and was described as a patriot, a champion for women, and a symbol of strength by Donald Trump upon her death.

23-year-old rugby player, who played for Bristol, has decided to leave the team at the end of the season to return to Wales and further develop his skills in a bid to secure a spot in the Welsh national team, with Newport Gwent Dragons also interested in signing him.

The article describes the trial of the people smugglers accused of transporting the Syrian family, including three-year-old Alan Kurdi, who tragically died attempting to cross to Greece, resulting in a global focus on the refugee crisis. The smugglers were found not guilty of causing death through deliberate negligence but were convicted of people smuggling. The Kurdi family's story continues to emphasize the ongoing migrant crisis, with thousands of refugees and migrants arriving daily in Greece from Turkey.

Former Milan station chief Robert Lady, convicted in absentia in 2009 for his role in the 2003 abduction and extraordinary rendition of an Egyptian cleric, was returned to the U.S. after his arrest in Panama in 2020, despite international search warrants and extradition requests from Italy. The practice of extraordinary rendition, moving suspects to countries where torture is permitted, has been widely condemned by human rights groups.

Passenger traffic increased at Edinburgh and Glasgow airports in January 2017, with Edinburgh reporting an 11.7% year-on-year increase, and Glasgow seeing an 8.4% rise. International flights in particular saw significant growth at both airports. Meanwhile, Aberdeen International Airport recorded its lowest decline in passenger numbers in nearly two years, but still saw a decrease of 1.7%. The article also mentions the growth of EU-scheduled traffic at Glasgow Airport, the increase in domestic traffic at both Edinburgh and Glasgow airports, and the commencement of new flights at Aberdeen Airport by Ryanair and Loganair.
The record-breaking video "Gangnam Style" by Psy has amassed over 9 quintillion views on YouTube, forcing the platform to update its video counter limitations.

"England, despite struggling in their opening matches, aim to win against Sri Lanka for a semi-finals spot in the World Twenty20, with Alex Hales' return likely, while Sri Lanka, previously defending champions who are struggling with their batting, are preparing to recover from a loss to face England."

Scotland's two largest cities, Edinburgh and Glasgow, rank second and third respectively among Britain's most congested cities, with anticipated costs of £2.8bn and £2.3bn in wasted time for Edinburgh and Glasgow drivers respectively over the next decade due to traffic congestion. If unaddressed, congestion levels across the UK could cost £61.8bn by 2025, with London having the most traffic "pinch points" in Europe, according to a study by Inrix Roadway Analytics.

In the 44th minute, Norway's Nordtveit scored an unexpected goal against Northern Ireland as his shot deflected off Sammy Clingan's heel, while in the second half, substitutes Elyounoussi, Ruud, and O'Neill's team contributed to Norway's 3-0 victory. Northern Ireland struggled to score, even during a frantic goalmouth scramble before half-time, and have not won more than one friendly in their last 14 matches.

Brussels remains on high alert due to fears of Paris-style attacks, with authorities conducting intensive patrols and several arrests made in connection to the Paris attacks. The suspected ringleader, Abdelhamid Abaaoud, who was later killed in police raids in Paris, had allegedly been planning an attack on the La Defense business district. An arrest warrant was issued for Mohamed Abrini, a suspect seen with Salah Abdeslam, who is the subject of an international manhunt, in connection to the Paris attacks. Both leaders, Francois Hollande of France and Barack Obama of the US, pledged to work together to eliminate the Islamic State group and increase co-operation to hit IS targets in Iraq and Syria.

There were coordinated terrorist attacks in Zaventem Airport, Brussels, and Maalbeek metro station on March 22, resulting in multiple deaths and injuries, prompting national mourning and increased security measures in several countries. The Islamic State has since claimed responsibility, potentially linking the incidents to the Paris attacks of November 2015.

Sheffield City Council has served a legal notice to Green Party Councillor, Alison Teal, threatening a High Court injunction for her continued involvement in tree-felling protests, citing months of alleged unlawful disruption to a 25-year tree management program, aimed at ensuring a better street scene and diverse tree stock.

Hundreds of whales have stranded at Farewell Spit, South Island, New Zealand, with many deaths; efforts to save survivors are ongoing, including the formation of a human chain to refloat them. This is one of the largest mass beachings in New Zealand's history, and the country has one of the highest stranding rates in the world, often occurring at Farewell Spit due to its shallow waters confounding whale navigation.

The Welsh rugby union team Ospreys have signed experienced prop forward Brian Mujati as injury cover for the sidelined Dmitri Arhip and Ma'afu Fia, with Rhodri Jones also unavailable due to Wales Six Nations duty. Mujati, who has played at top levels in Super Rugby, France's Top 14, and England's Premiership, is expected to provide valuable experience and bolster the squad during the remaining PRO12 games and Challenge Cup quarter-final.

The Gwynedd council plans to establish a new Church in Wales campus at Ysgol y Berwyn in Bala, despite 500 residents opposing the move and a previous dispute involving the church's support for the project. A report on the matter will be discussed at the council's cabinet meeting on 14th February, with the new three-to-19 campus expected to open in September 2018.

The article discusses a plan by Oxfordshire County Council to consolidate all services under one organization, potentially saving £100m over five years, although this proposal is met with opposition from district councils and city councils who favor either three separate councils or an elected mayor. The debate is criticized as a "turf war" over devolution plans, with arguments focusing on efficiency, accountability, and the unique needs of rural and urban areas within the county. Residents are being asked to provide input before the final proposal is presented to the county council's cabinet.

The Edinburgh rugby team is battling a challenging run-in, chasing a top-four finish in the table, with key matches against Newport Gwent Dragons, Zebre, Leinster, Munster, and Cardiff Blues. veteran player, Dickinson, feels all games must be won to have any chance of playoffs, despite recent poor form, which has been due to errors and loss of momentum resulting from international breaks according to Dickinson.

The Northern Ireland Bat Group, amidst a challenging summer, rescues grounded and injured bats, including those abandoned due to challenging weather conditions, and nurses them back to health before releasing them back into the wild. The volunteers' dedication is contributing significantly to the preservation of bats, an essential contributor to pest control and agriculture, contrary to common misconceptions about them.

The Supreme Court is currently considering a case that could limit the reach of federal law prohibiting gun ownership for individuals convicted of domestic violence, with Justice Clarence Thomas asking about the suspension of constitutional rights during a violation of any law.

Responsible Travel, a wildlife holiday specialist, is dropping about half a dozen trips involving zoos from their 3,500 options, as their boss, Justin Francis, finds these zoos inhumane and outdated, following the influence of a BBC TV program. The majority of the targeted zoos are in southeast Asia and none are in the UK. The decision is supported by the Born Free Foundation, which argues that animals often develop abnormal behavior in captivity and a global shift could significantly reduce the exploitation of wild animals in zoos worldwide.

A primary school-age child was found dead, leading to a 40-year-old woman's arrest on suspicion of murder in Faringdon, UK. Police are increasing their presence in the area as a precaution, seeking public assistance, and asking anyone with information to contact them.

A suspect in the UK is accused of breaching Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPim), reportedly the first such alleged violation, with the suspect alleged to have failed to contact a monitoring company and report to a police station twice in January. The Home Office refused to comment on the case, and those subject to a TPim can be ordered to report daily to a police station and adhere to other restrictions, with some arguing that TPims have weakened public protection against terrorism. The suspect has been granted unconditional bail, and the case is set for a plea and case management hearing on July 2.

Qualcomm, the world's largest chip supplier for smartphones, will reduce royalty rates on patents used in China's mobile phone market following a ruling that it violated the country's anti-monopoly law. The move could potentially benefit Chinese smartphone manufacturers Xiaomi and Huawei, as Qualcomm aims to remove uncertainty surrounding its business in China and focus on supporting its customers and partners in the region.

Michelle Mellotte, 61, a former doctor, has been stripped of her medical license after admitting to committing fraud and violating numerous fundamental principles of her profession, including endangering patients, bringing the profession into disrepute, and breaching professional ethics. She took £10,000 from an Alzheimer's patient in 2010, promising to repay it, but the money was not returned until a police investigation was initiated. She was suspended from the medical register and received a suspended prison sentence in April 2021.

A skeleton of a man aged between 30 and 49 years old, wearing a specific brand of clothing from 2008, was discovered at the M54 motorway in Shropshire, England. Police are unable to determine the cause of death and are not ruling out the possibility of a crime having occurred.

Archaeologists have discovered a previously unknown stone "square megalithic monument" at Avebury, one of Europe's largest stone circles, which is thought to be one of the site's earliest structures and potentially commemorates the ancestral home of the first people living in Avebury.

The Reading Borough Council has proposed to implement pay and display meters in certain areas including near the hospital, causing concern among hospital staff, residents, and university employees due to potential parking shortages and increased stress for patients and staff, with the council inviting public input on the plans by June 13th.

US Navy personnel, under increased scrutiny due to a series of incidents, are facing stricter alcohol policies and training following a three-car accident involving Petty Officer Aimee Mejia in Okinawa, which injured two people and resulted in Mejia's arrest for allegedly driving under the influence, six times the legal limit. The incident is adding fuel to longstanding local protests against the US military presence in Okinawa, as Prime Minister Abe urges stronger action from the US government.

A pair of young English batsmen, Duckett and Bell-Drummond, set the second highest List A partnership record of 367 runs, helping the Lions beat Sri Lanka A in a tri-series where they also defeated both Pakistan A and Sri Lanka A twice each. Their performances have caught the attention of coach Andy Flower, with Duckett's 220 not out being the ninth-highest List A score and Malan scoring 185 in another win, while Billings contributed a 175. Flower is optimistic that these players could have successful international careers.

The article states that Colombia's peace talks, suspended after rebels kidnapped Gen Ruben Dario Alzate and two others on 16 November, will resume in Havana from 10 December, with a focus on de-escalating the conflict and addressing victims' families, and aim to end five decades of conflict in which 220,000 people are estimated to have died. The captives were released and reunited with their families, and Gen Alzate resigned following the incident.

The Save Oxfordshire Children's Centres Campaign organized a "baby blockade" protest in Oxford against the Oxfordshire County Council's plans to cut the number of centres, aiming to save £8m, with a focus on replacing 44 existing centres with eight "children and family centres". The campaign invited former Prime Minister David Cameron to join the protest, noting his disappointment with the cuts, but received a response that the government continues to work with councils to make back-office savings and protect frontline services.

A controversial sandcastle depicting a murdered woman surrounded by police tape, constructed by Devon and Cornwall Police at a family beach event, was criticized as being offensive and insensitive due to its sexual stereotyping and trivialization of serious matters, particularly the reporting of sex crimes. The police apologized for any offense caused.

Leyton Orient's manager, Slade, has revealed plans for a revised club structure post-takeover and is eager to strengthen the squad, despite financially modest ambitions, aiming to improve on last season's performance and potentially secure promotion in the upcoming season.

The article summarizes that English golfer, Tommy Fleetwood, secured a spot at both The Open Championship and the USPGA Championship, achieved his best European Tour finish of second place, and earned a substantial payday in a Scottish Open tournament, despite a few missed birdie opportunities. He expressed satisfaction with the results and aims to qualify for the weekend at his next Open Championship.

The 10-year-old Irish-bred horse Many Clouds, known for its successful racing history and owned by Trevor Hemmings, tragically suffered a severe pulmonary haemorrhage after narrowly winning the Cotswold Chase at Cheltenham's Festival Trials Day, despite showing no significant underlying health issues or previous symptoms of ataxia. The British Horseracing Authority is determined to further investigate what causes such symptoms and potential prevention measures.

A 12-year-old girl testified at Sheffield Crown Court that she was sexually abused by Basharat Hussain and two others, and later raped by several men in Blackpool while, prosecutors allege, being orchestrated by Hussain. Hussain, along with six others, is on trial for alleged child abuse in Rotherham, including charges of rape and conspiracy to rape.

A 32-year-old motorcycle racer, Franck Petricola, tragically died at the TT after making a successful comeback from a serious accident at last year's North West 200. He was the 141st fatality at the races since they started in 1907, and an investigation is underway following the incident. Known for his resilience, Petricola had suffered multiple fractures and a head injury in a crash at the North West 200 in 2014 and had made a full recovery to compete at this year's event just last month.

Guy Martin, a popular racer, will not be returning to the Isle of Man TT due to a crash and mechanical issues with his Honda machine. Despite this, the event promises an exciting season with strong performances expected from Peter Hickman, Michael Dunlop, Dean Harrison, and other potential dark horses.

The article describes a disaster situation in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, following torrential rain flooding the region, resulting in the evacuation and rescue of more than 20,000 people, numerous road, home and infrastructure blockages, and thousands forced to seek shelter. The region has a history of dealing with extreme weather events, including a 2011 flood incident and the catastrophic impact of Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

The article reports that US Soccer has agreed to implement new safety measures in response to a concussion lawsuit, including limiting the amount of heading in practice for children aged 11-13 and modifications to substitution rules related to concussions. The FA in England has announced new guidelines on identifying, managing, and treating suspected head injuries in football but does not specify guidelines for children heading footballs and will present key research questions on the long-term effects of head injuries to Fifa.

Jerome Lavrilleux, a deputy director of former president Nicolas Sarkozy's 2012 presidential campaign, stated that Sarkozy was not aware of a financial "slip" involving almost 11 million euros in fake invoices, attributing the incident to a "terrible spiral" and a lack of emergency measures taken by those responsible. The scandal could potentially complicate any future election bids by Sarkozy.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders (CML) reported a decrease in home repossessions in the second quarter of the year, with 2,500 homes repossessed compared to 3,000 in the previous quarter and 5,400 in the same quarter last year. The decline was attributed to low interest rates, but the CML advised homeowners to prepare for a potential increase in interest rates. The number of homeowners and landlords in arrears also fell compared to the first quarter, according to CML figures. However, the number of tenants evicted by landlords rose by 4% in the second quarter. Shelter's chief executive suggested that rising rents and welfare cuts may have contributed to the increase in tenant evictions.

The article details that the city accepted 105 Syrian refugees between October and March as part of the UK's expanded resettlement programme, with costs covered by the UK Government. While this generated some controversy among politicians like UKIP MEP James Carver who claimed it put undue pressure on services in Coventry compared to other areas, local authorities overall showed a "tremendous amount of goodwill". Notably, none of the refugees were placed in the North West, and only three were settled in areas such as Kingston upon Thames and Mid Sussex. The Home Office plans to resettle 20,000 Syrian refugees by 2020 as part of its Syrian Vulnerable Persons Resettlement Scheme.

Brazil's President Dilma Rousseff assures that the 2016 Rio Olympics, despite various challenges such as economic crises, delays in construction, and water pollution, will bring honor and pride, ensuring a safe and successful event, and inviting fans from previous visitations like the football World Cup. The torch relay for the Olympics will travel through 300 Brazilian cities, and officials state that despite water pollution concerns in the Guanabara Bay, athletes will not be at risk during the August 2016 games.

Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi's reform measure, approved by the lower house of parliament, guarantees a majority of seats to the party winning the most votes in an election, with the aim of ending Italy's era of unstable coalitions and establishing a more stable governance model. Critics argue that the reform gives too much power to single parties, reduces voter choice, and threatens democratic norms.

The 20-year-old Ajax footballer, Abdelhak Nouri, is diagnosed with severe brain damage following heart rhythm problems during a game in Austria, with the prognosis for recovery being grim, according to a club statement.

Swansea earned a crucial win, following a string of losses, in a match where Jordan Ayew scored for Villa Park but was answered by Sigurdsson's free-kick and a winning goal by Jordan's brother, Andre. This victory lifted Swansea out of their slump, providing improved morale and adding confidence in preparation for their home game against Arsenal.

A Polish mother is requesting help from Costa coffee shop customers and employees to locate her 10-year-old son who has been missing since early this year, as he is believed to be in the UK with his British father and often frequented Costa coffee shops, and her legal representative is appealing for information to ensure the boy's safety and reunite him with his mother.

New US travel rules require dual citizens from Iran, Iraq, Syria, and Sudan to apply for a visa at the US embassy instead of using the visa waiver scheme, angering these nationalities and causing confusion due to unclear implementation guidelines.

Sky is working to increase capacity at telephone exchanges in areas experiencing issues, coinciding with the launch of Sky Go Extra, a service for offline movie and TV show downloads. The expert suggests this service might strain the network further, especially as Sky's network traffic has risen due to increased customer additions, causing capacity challenges in some exchanges. Subscribers can check if their local exchange is affected using an online postcode checking facility.

A Liverpool gang led by Joseph McHale, Kevin Schruyers, and Robin Vaughan was convicted for a series of ATM robberies in Scotland between August and November 2013. The gang, using explosives to access safes behind the ATMs, was responsible for incidents in multiple towns and thefts totaling over £133,000. Robin Vaughan admitted his involvement in the crimes, while McHale and Schruyers were also found guilty of attempting to break into an ATM in Mintlaw. The investigation ultimately traced the group to Liverpool due to the presence of Scottish banknotes with telltale signs of dye in the Mersey area.

The Scottish Prison Service has announced the use of new technology to interfere with mobile phone signals at two pilot sites (HMP Shotts and Glenochil) as part of efforts to combat the use of contraband phones, which have been linked to criminal activities such as drug supply, organized crime, and harassment. The technology is expected to become operational within weeks and could serve as a model for future installations.

Former French President Francois Hollande attended a ceremony to mark 70 years since the liberation of the last Nazi camps, emphasizing the importance of knowledge in preventing future atrocities, as France and other countries face a resurgence of attacks targeting Jewish and Muslim communities. Meanwhile, Germany commemorated the 70th anniversary of the liberation of Bergen-Belsen, where Anne Frank perished, while Croatia honored survivors of the Jasenovac camp.

Johnny Depp, 52, and Amber Heard, 30, have filed for divorce in Los Angeles Superior Court, citing irreconcilable differences after 15 months of marriage. The celebrity couple, who have no children, have recently faced court proceedings in Australia over allegations of illegal dog importation, resulting in a war of words spanning months, including disputes about the dogs' welfare and insults such as Depp calling Deputy Prime Minister Barnaby Joyce "inbred with a tomato."

The Maersk Tigris, a container ship carrying a multinational crew, is currently held by Iranian authorities in their waters, according to Iranian media, due to an alleged debt complaint from a private Iranian company. The crew remains safe and the U.S. Navy is monitoring the situation, after a distress call was picked up by U.S. Naval Forces, following an incident where Iranian Revolutionary Guards Navy patrol vessels approached the ship and fired warning shots.

The article discusses a call made by Sarah Pollock, seeking the disclosure of the full Seren Bernard case review report from 2014, which details her death at age 14 in foster care in Pembrokeshire in 2012. The council refused the request, citing legal advice, despite acknowledging the desire for transparency to provide opportunities for learning from such tragic incidents. Pollock remains dissatisfied, expressing feelings of trauma and unanswered questions due to the limited information she has received.

In a Super League game, Leigh dominated Salford, scoring 18 points in the first half and further extending their lead in the second to secure a decisive 24-0 victory. Their win meant Widnes Vikings finished at the bottom of the table. Salford's performance dip in the latter stages of the season resulted in them dropping from third to fourth place, missing a 40-year record-breaking league placing. Both teams will now participate in the Super League 8 qualifiers. Leigh's coach Neil Jukes was pleased with his team's game management, defense, and energy, while Salford's coach Ian Watson expressed disappointment in his team's performance and called for a renewed focus on the intensity and hunger shown earlier in the season.

Paul Allen and Burt Rutan, aided by Elon Musk's space company, are building a gigantic aircraft capable of launching unmanned rockets into space, offering launch flexibility, minimizing weather constraints, and saving rocket fuel, with potential applications for the commercial satellite industry and the International Space Station.

Lancashire set Derbyshire a challenging target of 365 in a first-class match, with Alex Davies (89) and Simon Kerrigan (17 not out) adding valuable runs, while Derbyshire lost two wickets in their initial innings, leaving them struggling at 27-2, with Peter Siddle and Tom Bailey taking the wickets of Ben Slater and Billy Godleman. Both teams are optimistic about their chances for the remainder of the match, with Lancashire confident that their bowlers can knock over Derbyshire and Alex Davies expressing that a lead of 250-260 is not a substantial enough margin. Derbyshire's Tom Taylor is also hopeful, emphasizing the importance of forming big partnerships and the potential of the ball continuing to swing.

Jon Stewart, a renowned American satirist and the voice of liberal America, concluded his 17-year stint as host of The Daily Show, with guests such as Bruce Springsteen, John Kerry, and John McCain in attendance. His final monologue expressed gratitude to colleagues, fans, and family, emphasizing that the show was not ending but pausing, and departing with a quip about getting a drink. The Daily Show, which has been influential for young viewers, has launched the careers of several famous comedians, including Steve Carell, John Oliver, and Stephen Colbert, among others. #JonVoyage trended on Twitter as fans, including McCain, paid tribute to Stewart as he bid farewell.

Forest, who have failed to advance past the third round of the cup competition in the past 11 seasons, aim to qualify again and potentially secure a spot in the Europa League, starting their campaign against League Two side Doncaster.

The Arches nightclub, a significant cultural venue in Glasgow, went into administration after a midnight closing time was imposed due to drug abuse and disorder incidents, putting 130 jobs at risk. The Scottish government has pledged support, with Creative Scotland providing immediate funding and exploring long-term options for arts programming. Efforts are being made to address the closure and potentially reopen the venue.

In 1972, Jean McConville, a mother-of-10, was kidnapped by the IRA, accused of being an informant, and was later found dead in 2003. On Tuesday, Ivor Bell, a senior IRA leader in the 1970s, was arrested for aiding and abetting her murder and membership of the IRA. He was part of an IRA delegation that held secret talks with the British government in 1972, including Gerry Adams and Martin McGuinness. McConville was one of the Disappeared, a term for those abducted, murdered, and secretly buried by republicans during the Troubles. Although the IRA admitted to murdering and burying nine of the Disappeared in 1999, the remains of seven, including McConville, have not been found to this day.

Wigan Warriors overcame a 12-man disadvantage to score 21 unanswered points and beat Catalans Dragons, demonstrating resilience and securing crucial confidence for the remainder of the season. Despite the victory, Wigan's hopes for the League Leaders' Shield are slim, and they must focus on a home semi-final by winning their next game against Catalans Dragons. If Wigan reaches the final for the fourth consecutive season, they may be without Ben Flower due to his red card and subsequent suspension.

The Yorkshire Sculpture Park has seen a massive 170% increase in visitor numbers during September due to the installation of the poppy sculpture "Wave," attracting 100,000 people compared to 37,000 last year. This Nationwide tour of poppies is an extension of the "Blood Swept Lands and Seas of Red" artwork from London, which marked 100 years since the start of World War One and drew over five million visitors. The sculpture, known for its "calm and contemplative experience," is expected to make the park's year its biggest ever, with more than half a million visitors.

A severe flood warning on the A361 between East Lyng and Burrowbridge was lifted on March 10th following inspections and clearance work, despite some remaining water on the road, temporary traffic lights were installed. Local authorities thanked their teams for their efforts, urging caution due to filled-up rhynes and foggy conditions. The A372 Langport Road remains closed for flood pump removal next week, while the large pumps at Beer Wall are no longer needed due to improving weather. After pump removal, the road will close for further flood damage assessment and emergency repairs.

The article reports that scientists have discovered an icy body, V774104, likely 15.5 billion kilometers from the Sun, significantly further out than Pluto, using Japan's Subaru telescope. The object is estimated to be 500-1,000 kilometers in size and its orbit needs to be further tracked. The discovery was made by a team led by Scott Sheppard and Chad Trujillo, who specialize in detecting Solar System outliers. The previously recognized most distant object is Eris, with V7741b's trajectory in the Solar System remaining uncertain.

A primary school headteacher, Ashley Yates, has admitted to using a spy pen to record indecent images of children and staff at The Tynings Primary School, South Gloucestershire. Further investigations have uncovered additional adult victims. Police continue their enquiries and Yates remains in custody until his next court hearing on 9th August. School officials are working closely with authorities to provide information and support to those affected.

British rowers Helen Glover and Heather Stanning, the unbeaten world champions, won their second consecutive Olympic gold in the women's pair in Rio, leading from the start with a time of 7 minutes 18.29 seconds, 1.2 seconds clear of New Zealand, and setting a record of 39 races unbeaten.

Steve, a presenter on CBBC's Deadly 60, and his Strictly Come Dancing partner Ola assert that they were misrepresented in a bullying allegation, and they maintained their unity and professionalism throughout the situation. They expressed that it was a difficult experience, but they handled it by maintaining a positive attitude and focusing on their dance performances. They also encouraged people affected by bullying to seek help.

Inflation dropped from 2.9% to 2.6% in June, reducing expectations for a near-term interest rate hike, which sent the pound down against the dollar and euro, but initially boosted the FTSE 100 before closing down 13.91 points, while Royal Mail shares increased due to a 1% revenue rise.

Nottingham-born actress Vicky McClure, famously recognized by her tram on the Nottingham city network, shared an uncomfortable story on The Graham Norton Show about her tram ride in 2015. She and her mother were offered a free ride after a ceremony to unveil the tram, but later challenged by a conductor. Despite presenting the plaque she received at the ceremony, the pair were thrown off for fare evasion, though Nottingham Express Transit acknowledged it was an "unfortunate misunderstanding."

The inquest inquires into the death of 14-year-old Alice Gross in West London, considering whether government and police failures contributed to her death and addressing the circumstances that allowed suspected killer Arnis Zalkalns, who had a conviction for murder in Latvia, to live unchecked in the UK. Alice's family seeks to establish if systems for monitoring foreign offenders and cross-border information sharing are robust and emphasizes the need to prevent similar occurrences in the future.

The study conducted by The Local Data Company (LDC) and the University of Stirling shows that the average retail vacancy rate in Scotland dropped from 14.5% to 13.7%, with East Kilbride having the highest vacancy rate (33%) and Inverurie the lowest (1%). About 40% of empty shops have been vacant for more than three years, and town vacancy rates have improved at a quicker pace than cities. The most improved towns included Anstruther, Clydebank, Dumfries, Inverkeithing, Lochgelly, Peterhead, and Pitlochry, while diversity, leisure, and charity shops varied significantly across towns and cities. Matthew Hopkinson, LDC director, emphasized the significance of the high vacancy rates, implying potential obsolescence and a challenge for healthy and sustainable communities.

Rory McWhirter, from Edinburgh, used fake identities obtained from tricking people into applying for nonexistent jobs at a Glasgow hotel to produce falsified birth certificates, which he then used to claim thousands in tax credits, child benefits, and a Sure Start maternity grant before his scheme was exposed. His solicitor stated he planned the scam to fund a property business upon which he had already spent £80,000 and could pay back the defrauded sum with £2,000 to £2,500 monthly installments if not imprisoned. However, the court, finding his actions sustained "attacks" on the public purse, the integrity of birth, death, and marriage documentation, and the working tax credit, child benefit, and maternity grant systems, ruled that a prison term was necessary.

The authorities in Saudi Arabia have been trying to demolish the old Shia quarter of Awamiya since May, with activists alleging that this effort is to forcibly displace residents, while accusing security forces of firing randomly at homes and cars, resulting in clashes that have left at least seven people dead. The region, where the majority are Shia, has been experiencing increased unrest since 2011, with protests and attacks becoming more frequent following the 2016 execution of the prominent Shia cleric Nimr al-Nimr. This situation has led to accusations from activists that security forces are opening fire on demonstrators, jailing, or sentencing them to death for protest-related crimes.

The article discusses young adults in Belfast expressing frustration over the struggle to find employment, criticizing the election-focused behavior of politicians and calling for improved job opportunities, training programs, and political focus on issues beyond elections.

Andrew Travers, Barnet Council's Chief Executive, stepped down after a polling error led to the exclusion of voters in the borough during the EU Referendum, with an independent investigation launching to review the incident's appropriateness and make recommendations for future elections.

Manager Neil Warnock has extended an offer to midfielder Peter Whittingham for a new contract, allowing him time to consider it, while hinting that his long-term plans do not include Emyr Huws and Stuart O'Keefe, who have since moved on loan.

The article discusses a BBC and BuzzFeed News investigation revealing suspected match-fixing in elite tennis, with tennis player Andy Fleming expressing concern and urging strict punishments, emphasizing the importance of sport's purity and fairness, and stating he has no knowledge of any match-fixing in the ongoing Australian Open.

A 60-year-old man walked into a bank on Bristol Road South in Northfield, reportedly producing a firearm without making any threats or demands. He was later taken to hospital for a psychiatric evaluation and is expected to be questioned about suspected firearms offences. Police contained the scene, negotiated with the man, and no customers or staff were harmed in the incident.

Mohammed Ali, a 31-year-old software programmer from Liverpool, has denied attempting to possess a deadly toxin (ricin) after allegedly ordering it online, pretending to be "Weirdos 0000." The supposed deal was actually a sting operation carried out by the FBI, who had been posing as the supplier. The trial is ongoing, with the defense suggesting Ali's actions were driven by his interest in pushing technological boundaries, possibly influenced by the TV series "Breaking Bad."

Newport County football club, tenants of Rodney Parade stadium, are facing criticism from rugby team manager Westley over the quality of the football pitch, which Davies, CEO of Rodney Parade Limited, states is being repaired but lacks a immediate solution due to high costs.

Nearly 7 out of 10 people surveyed admitted to working while unwell, with concerns about backlogged work upon return, while only a quarter admitted to taking sick days when healthy. The survey highlights the issue of presenteeism, where employees attend work ill, posing a potential threat to productivity and morale.

The Bank of England cut its growth forecast for 2017, held interest rates at 0.25%, and a vote for a rate rise was not implemented as expected; Sterling dropped against both the dollar and euro; FTSE 100 closed almost flat despite sterling's fall, helped by mining shares; Fresnillo, Randgold Resources, and Antofagasta rallied, while Hikma plummeted due to US regulatory delay in drug approval; Centrica, BT, and Mondi dropped due to various reasons including regulatory concerns, weak earnings, and sliding profits.

Russian hacker and son of a Russian MP, Roman Seleznev, was found guilty of operating a credit card theft scheme targeting US pizza chains in Washington state between 2008 and 2014. He faces a mandatory four-year jail term, following his arrest and extradition, and a conviction on 38 out of 40 charges. His lawyers plan to appeal the conviction, citing illegal arrest and the use of evidence from a corrupted laptop. The US Department of Justice responded by stating that Seleznev was prosecuted for his conduct, not his nationality. The Russian government has lodged official complaints regarding Seleznev's seizure and extradition, alleging a US campaign to "hunt" Russians worldwide.

The president, under pressure to produce alleged recordings following an inquiry into Russian election interference and after he requested James Comey drop an investigation, denied their existence in a tweet. However, Comey had previously stated that he was asked by the president to let go of any possible prosecution of former National Security Adviser Mike Flynn and hinted he hopes there are recordings of their conversation.

Liberty, led by Sanjeev Gupta, has expressed interest in acquiring Tata Steel's UK assets, including Port Talbot, Newport, Rotherham, Corby, Shotton, and Teesside. Liberty has already shown interest in other Tata Steel plants and has been focusing on recycling scrap metal for steel production. A potential competitor, Excalibur Steel UK Limited, is also preparing a bid. The UK government has promised support for any potential buyer, including a potential 25% stake in a new business and financial aid. Tata Steel has indicated it cannot continue indefinitely without a deal due to heavy losses.

Nottingham area trams are planned to extend to East Midlands Airport, Toton's HS2 station, and potentially Derby, with regional councils advocating for this as a priority project in devolution negotiations, although specific costs and timelines are not yet disclosed.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, the five-time world champion, equalized Stephen Hendry's record for most Masters wins and recorded the biggest-ever margin of victory (9-0) in a Masters final by modifying his game, citing inspiration from young players like Neil Robertson, Judd Trump, and Ding Junhui, which boosts his self-belief and confidence.

Extremely destructive storms killed six people, damaged thousands of homes, and destroyed vast forests, including rare habitats, in Poland; officials estimate eight million cubic meters of lumber were lost, making it the worst forest disaster in Polish and possibly European history. The disaster occurred in the northern and western regions, with Torun alone losing over 23,000 hectares of forest. The Polish government faces intense criticism for logging in Europe's oldest forest, Bialowieza, a UNESCO World Heritage site that is home to rare wildlife. The European Court of Justice will determine the fate of ongoing logging operations in the coming months.

renowned Latin singer Enrique Iglesias had to undergo a more extensive procedure than anticipated, including a fracture correction and reconstructive surgery on his injured hand, after an accident during a concert where he attempted to grab a drone camera and suffered a laceration on his fingers; he is expected to recover fully and resume his tour on July 3rd.

In the Super League match, Leeds Rhinos defeated Warrington Wolves 24-0 with Matt Parcell scoring a hat-trick and Joel Moon scoring his 15th try in 16 games. Warrington made numerous handling errors, and the closest they came to scoring was a Joe Philbin try that was held up over the line. Leeds head coach Brian McDermott commented on the performance, expressing satisfaction with the clean sheet but acknowledging that the team was playing a struggling Warrington side. Warrington head coach Tony Smith attributed the loss to poor execution, forcing mistakes, and weak kicking game.

William (Plum) Smith, a former paramilitary and PUP leader, played a central role in the 1994 ceasefire of loyalist paramilitary groups, particularly by chairing a press conference for the Combined Loyalist Military Command. He was a key figure in bringing loyalist paramilitaries into the peace process and was noted for his intelligence, progressive political views, and efforts to represent working-class individuals. He passed away, with tributes paid by prominent figures such as Martin McGuinness and Brian Ervine.

Olive Cooke, a 92-year-old resident of Bristol, has been an avid supporter of the Royal British Legion (RBL) for over 75 years, starting her involvement while still a teenager. As a long-standing poppy collector, she sells poppies at the entrance to Bristol Cathedral, and her dedication to the cause is deeply personal, stemming from the loss of her first husband in World War II. The RBL acknowledges her as their "most-valued poppy collector" and appreciates her longstanding support during the Poppy Appeal.

Israeli statesman Shimon Peres, a key figure in the founding of Israel and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate for his efforts in resolving the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, passed away after a stroke at the age of 93. His political career spanned more than six decades and included roles as prime minister, president, and, early on, defense minister. Notable achievements include securing deals for arms and aircraft, founding Israel's nuclear facility, and overseeing the successful rescue of hostages from a hijacked plane in 1976. Later in his career, he became a leading advocate for peace and compromise in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, emphasizing the need for diplomacy and mutual understanding.

The BBC reported that a major survey conducted at Queen's University in Northern Ireland, with over 70% participation, found that only 29% of staff agreed on effective leadership, while ratings were generally positive regarding change management, job satisfaction, university standing, and commitment to world-class research. However, staff were skeptical about change resulting from the survey. The university responded by acknowledging the survey results, emphasizing staff engagement, and committing to developing action plans to address challenges and build on identified strengths.

The X-47B jet, being developed by Northrop Grumman, had its maiden flight reaching an altitude of 5,000 feet for 29 minutes. Its tailless stealth design, similar to the B-2 Stealth Bomber, aims to create a new generation of radar-invisible, faster unmanned drones, different from current remote-controlled planes like the Predator and Reaper. The X-47B is part of a £395 million contract and is expected to undergo further tests, including its first one from an aircraft carrier in 2013.

Airbus announces reduced production of the double-deck A380 aircraft, acknowledges disappointing second-quarter profits, struggling with delays in US engine-maker Pratt & Whitney's engines for A320neo aircraft, and is having constructive talks with Qatar Airways over their recent cancellation of four A350 aircraft orders.

The Dongsha Atoll in the South China Sea has experienced a 40% coral death rate, the highest in at least 40 years, according to expert Anne Cohen. Cohen attributes this to the 2015/2016 El Nino which caused devastating bleaching in several coral reefs globally, not just the Great Barrier Reef. The high local weather conditions caused a 6-degree Celsius spike in temperature due to a high-pressure system, which is more severe than the suggested 2-degree Celsius threshold and shows predictions for coral reef preservation may be overly optimistic for shallow waters.

Scientists at the University of Queensland and Monash University developed a protein, Hi1a, from Australian funnel web spider venom, which showed promising results in reducing brain damage in laboratory rats during stroke simulations. While the research is in its early stages, it holds potential for future stroke treatment.

In a football match between Oldham and Bradford, Oldham took an early lead with a Peter Clarke header from a free-kick. Despite Bradford dominating the rest of the game, the score remained 1-0 at half-time. Bradford equalized via a penalty kick after a foul by Ousmane Fane, and despite continued dominance, Bradford were unable to take the lead. The game ended in a 1-1 draw, with Bradford scoring another penalty late in the second half after a foul by Ryan Flynn.

The article reports that a study has shown the experimental drug aducanumab, which targets the build-up of amyloid in the brain, is safe to take and exhibits positive effects on memory in early-stage Alzheimer's patients. However, the drug produced side effects like headaches, and larger phase 3 studies combining 2,700 patients are currently underway to further evaluate its cognitive decline effects. Experts are cautiously optimistic but note that past Alzheimer's drug development has had many disappointments.

In the Challenge Cup, Oldham Roughyeds, currently fourth from bottom in the second tier, led 24-6 at halftime against Hull Kingston Rovers, a Super League side. Despite a comeback attempt from Hull KR in the second half, Oldham held on to win 24-22. Hull KR's coach described their performance as an "utter embarrassment."

Tony Hall, the director general of the BBC, plans to make the BBC an "open BBC for the internet age" by creating a children's iPlayer, a pool of local reporters who will share work with local newspapers, an Ideas Service, and allowing third-party content on the iPlayer. However, these initiatives will be contingent on funding cuts, which might lead to the loss or reduction of some services. The plans are a response to critics who accuse the corporation of being "imperial in its ambitions". The BBC's proposals for local reporters have been met with criticism by the Scottish Newspaper Society and the News Media Association, who argue that it would undermine local news publishing and further concentrate news coverage in the hands of the state-funded broadcaster.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission, in a letter to party leaders, expresses concern over increasing hate attacks in the UK since the Brexit vote, calling for accurate information and respectful debate. It points to a rise in hate crimes, including the murder of Jo Cox, racist, anti-Semitic, and homophobic attacks, and the pulling off of hijabs, as "stains on our society". The commission urges all politicians to be mindful of their impact on national mood and suggests reviewing hate crime sentences in England and Wales.

Ms. Evans, who served as the author of UKIP's 2015 general election manifesto and was briefly suspended for bringing the party into disrepute, has expressed interest in running for the party's leadership but is unable to due to allegations against her that she has dismissed and a party rulebook she claims has been abused. Despite this, she supports councillor Lisa Duffy as the best candidate to lead the party to change and growth, envisioning a more unified, consensual UKIP that breaks free from its hard-right image and, under Duffy's leadership, becomes more like a political party than a club.

The changes to the English GCSE system will involve a new grading system using numbers instead of letters, scrapping coursework for most subjects, and returning to two-year linear assessments. This will initially apply to English language, English literature, maths, and start from the autumn of 2015. Other popular GCSE subjects will follow suit by 2018. Scotland and Northern Ireland will not be affected, while Wales is planning its own GCSE shake-up. The new system aims to raise expectations and improve core skills in English and maths, but there are concerns about the potential negative impact on less able students and the confusion caused by the blend of numbered and traditional letter grades.

Gen. Petraeus, who resigned as CIA director in 2012 due to an extramarital affair, expressed willingness to serve under President Trump, stating that personal reservations should be set aside if it benefits the country. He suggested that Trump could forge closer ties with Russia, drawing parallels with President Nixon's overtures to China in the 1970s. However, he cautioned against any such efforts without careful consideration.

Supporters of Egypt's new President Mohammed Mursi, of the Muslim Brotherhood, are in a standoff with generals who have ruled since the ouster of Hosni Mubarak. During a meeting with President Mursi, Secretary of State Hillary Clinton urged compromise and real politics, while also praising Egypt's military council for its interim leadership. Clinton aims to support Egypt's democratic transition while encouraging Mursi to address issues like the peace treaty with Israel and the protection of women and minorities.

Derek Bruder testified about his encounter with West Midlands Police officer Matthew Sawers in 1990, during which he was allegedly pressured to change his story about the vital signs of 15-year-old Kevin Williams, who perished in the 1989 Hillsborough disaster. However, Sawers denies applying pressure or altering the sense of Bruder's statement. The inquests continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the 96 lives lost during the FA Cup semi-final between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest.

The article discusses the journey of the British musical duo Oh Wonder, who experienced sudden fame after their self-released songs, including Body Gold, became an online phenomenon, eventually leading to a record deal and an extensive world tour. To maintain anonymity due to injury and their belief in "art over artist", they used a vocal technique where both musicians sing in unison, becoming known for their unique sound. Post-tour, they penned their upcoming album Ultralife, which they say reflects the ability of certain people to pull one out of difficult moments and into a positive, empowered state. The duo prefers to keep their personal lives private and has not confirmed romantic involvement.

Bertrand Traore scored a goal for Chelsea against Stoke City, but Diouf's header after Courtois's mistake leveled the match for the Potters. Stoke remained seventh in the table, with Chelsea 10th. Chelsea fielded a weakened lineup for the game, with to meet PSG in Champions League and Everton in FA Cup. Both teams ended the game with a point.

The research of William C Campbell, Satoshi Omura, and Youyou Tu has led to the development of drugs to treat malaria, onchocerciasis (river blindness), and lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis), diseases affecting over 3.4 billion people worldwide. Their work has been instrumental in the development of ivermectin to combat the roundworm parasites causing the latter two diseases, and the discovery of artemisinin for malaria treatment. However, resistance to these drugs is emerging, necessitating continued research for new treatments.

The Nelson Mandela Foundation, led by associates of South Africa's first black president, has called out current leader Jacob Zuma for allegedly prioritizing private interests over state affairs, looting resources, and using key institutions to further personal interests, which is threatening South Africa's democracy. The foundation's statement comes as a court hearing begins on Zuma's legal team's bid to stop the release of a corruption report from former anti-corruption chief Thuli Madonsela, who investigated allegations of influence wielded by the wealthy Gupta family in Zuma's government. Both Zuma and the Guptas continue to deny any wrongdoing, and Zuma's legal team argues that the report's release would be unlawful as he was not given enough time to respond to allegations. The foundation also echoes growing calls, including from opposition parties, for the report's publication and for Zuma to face impeachment again if the report contains adverse findings.

The comedian and actress, Miranda, performed her signature gallop during the curtain call of the musical "Annie" at London's Piccadilly Theatre, making her West End debut as the "big and brash and clowny" orphanage owner, receiving positive reviews for her performance, while the show's unashamed optimism is seen as a comfort during current times.

Geographically signed midfielder Jonjo Shelvey, who joined from Swansea for £12m, contributed to both goals in a 2-1 victory for Newcastle over West Ham, rising to 16th place in the league. The Magpies squandered opportunities but held on for the win, with keeper Rob Elliot making a key save in the 90th minute to preserve the victory. Steve McClaren emerged victorious against former England manager Slaven Bilic, who expressed disappointment over his team's performance.

Supermarkets Morrisons, Tesco, Asda, and Sainsbury's cut diesel prices by up to 2p per litre due to lower wholesale costs, with diesel potentially reaching parity with petrol since July 2001 prices based on Experian Catalyst analysis. The RAC suggests this trend is influenced by increased diesel supply from overseas refineries and a stronger pound against the US dollar.

The 70th UN General Assembly, a key gathering for African leaders, is a venue mixing diplomacy, shopping, immunity from prosecution, and crucial discussions regarding peacekeeping, corruption allegations, and humanitarian concerns like hunger and poverty. This year, the SDGs, intended to replace the Millennium Goals, are presented with a special focus on ending hunger, a persistent issue exacerbated by climate change, food shortages, and political instability in various African nations. The UN is both criticized as an overstaffed, Western-influenced bureaucracy and praised as a necessary lifeline for those in need across the continent.

The police are warning about potentially deadly Superman logo pills containing PMMA still circulating, as experts warn not to assume a different logo means the drug is safe, and there's no reliable way to tell if a pill contains PMMA.

Former Leave.EU campaign chairman Mr Banks urged current UKIP leader Paul Nuttall to re-involve ex-leader Nigel Farage in the party, claiming he is UKIP's "biggest asset," and proposed a new leadership structure to make the party more efficient and relevant again. However, Mr Nuttall's political advisor, Patrick O'Flynn, responded negatively to suggestions of donor involvement in party leadership decisions.

The article discusses a service called Invisible Girlfriend/Boyfriend, where for a fee, you can create a fictional relationship on social media or receive text messages from an online persona to make it seem like you have a girlfriend or boyfriend. Thousands of users pay for this service, using it for various reasons such as getting parents off their backs, escaping unwanted advances, or practicing flirting. The service takes the illusion seriously, providing tips and even live chat support.

Germany displayed a dominant offensive performance against Poland, demonstrating their formidable arsenal of attacking weapons led by Thomas Muller, Karim Bellarabi, and Bastian Schweinsteiger, but revealed occasional lapses in concentration, presenting a potential opportunity for Scotland in an upcoming match.

In a match where on-loan striker Tammy Abraham missed a chance to secure Bristol City's victory, Rovers' Sam Gallagher scored a late header to secure a 1-1 draw for Blackburn, keeping them two points from safety with only three games remaining in the season. Bristol City created numerous opportunities but were unable to hold onto their lead, while Blackburn complained about a penalty decision not given in their favor.

Scotland's number eight Strauss expresses the team's desire to send coach Cotter off with a win in the upcoming Six Nations match against Ireland, as they face Ireland's dominant side which has defeated South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand since last summer. Despite Scotland's inexperienced front-row, Ireland captain Rory Best expects a battle in the set-pieces.

John Guidetti scored a free-kick resulting from Pascali's red card foul on Stefan Scepovic, with Conor Brennan making multiple saves for Kilmarnock; Scepovic added a second after the break, but Brennan's efforts were not enough to prevent a 2-0 loss against Celtic.

The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) study reveals that Northern Irish students have a high level of life satisfaction compared to their peers worldwide, but experience high levels of test anxiety, bullying, and extended internet use, which can negatively impact their well-being. The study also found that Northern Irish students have stronger relationships with their parents, teachers, and harbor a strong academic drive, which contributes to their academic performance and overall satisfaction.

In an unexpected turn of events, Crystal Palace, initially struggling against a dominant Everton side, seized the initiative after Romelu Lukaku's early goal. Palace equalized through a Mile Jedinak penalty, countered with Fraizer Campbell's header and Yannick Bolasie's low shot to take control of the game. Everton managed to score a penalty late in the game through Leighton Baines, but Palace held on for a 3-2 victory. The match showcased Palace's resilience and tactical acumen under manager Neil Warnock.

Freelance sports journalist Gary Carter, who was covering a rugby league match, suffered head injuries in an altercation in London and was admitted to the Royal London Hospital for surgery to remove a blood clot from his brain. His wife reported that he was heavily sedated due to swelling on the brain. A 35-year-old man has been charged with causing grievous bodily harm, and both a 22-year-old and another individual were arrested in connection with the incident. The England team and fellow sports figures offered their support and well wishes for a full recovery.

British artist Tinie Tempah, with seven number one singles in this decade, discusses his pristine studio where he created his million-selling debut album Disc-Overy, and where he's been working on his third album, Youth, for over two years. He credits the delays in completing the album to losing touch with his roots, which he reconnected with by meeting up with friends and doing things he enjoyed before fame. The new album, Youth, exhibits a playful warmth that was missing from his second album Demonstration. Tempah reflects on the changes in the music industry, highlighting the success of self-reliant British artists like Skepta and Stormzy who've achieved major success with their own labels. He values his artistic progression and the ability to tell stories through music, even if it means missing out on certain life experiences. Tempah's album Youth is set to be released on 14 April.

The article discusses plans for accelerating the allocation of radio spectrum to allow mobile operators like O2 and Vodafone to launch 4G networks, with a potential launch in summer 2013. However, the process is being delayed due to legal challenges and negotiations involving all the networks, as rival network EE has already been granted permission to use its existing spectrum for 4G services. Apple's latest iPhone is available on all major networks but can only offer 4G speeds on EE's network. The decision to allow EE to launch 4G earlier has been controversial among other operators, who argue it gives EE a headstart in the 4G market.

The Conservative government has decided to scrap a policy offering free school lunches for children in the first three years of primary school, a move previously criticized as too expensive and impractical, sparking resentment among teachers and school heads who attest to its positive impact on students and school culture.

A suspect, believed to be an Israeli Arab, opened fire in a busy part of Tel Aviv on a Friday afternoon, injuring several civilians in a bar and cafe, triggering a massive manhunt by Israeli security forces. The motive for the shooting is unclear, with speculation ranging from terrorism to hate crimes or organized crime, but the incident is the latest in a recent wave of Palestinian attacks against Israelis.

Musical artist Dean Owens discovering his great great grandfather Ambrose Salvona was buried in Inverness, Scotland, was confirmed after a local resident offered to help, and subsequently, the grave was found in Tomnahurich Cemetery. This discovery influenced Owens' songwriting, particularly in the track 'Dora' from his Nashville-recorded album Into the Sea, which tells the story of his grandmother who grew up in a circus started by Salvona in Scotland. The song includes verses about Salvona's life as a lion tamer and his arrival in Scotland with a dancing bear in the late 19th Century. Local historians have since uncovered more details about Salvona's life, including two marriages and the birth of at least 10 children.

The article discusses the introduction of sustainable, recycled stainless steel pint cups atGlastonbury Festival, which is a first on such a major scale, albeit without a logo or other identifying mark. The cups are durable but challenging to throw, and are not compulsory. The cups are made from 80% recycled steel, which is part of the festival's larger effort towards sustainability. The cups are expected to reduce waste and encourage a reusable revolution, though they may present a challenge in recycling due to the lack of a standard marking system.

A 15-year-old boy in Nepal miraculously survived a banquet collapsed during the earthquake by drinking water from wet clothes and eating clarified butter, while rescue efforts continued across the region, with helicopters playing a crucial role in delivering aid to remote villages. Even as people returned to their homes and shops reopened in some parts of Kathmandu, frustration mounted over the slow pace of relief efforts in some rural areas, with the death toll rising to 6,130 and over eight million people affected. The UN estimates that 70,000 houses were destroyed. The rescue of a woman and an 11-year-old girl from the rubble, along with reports of people suffering from waterborne illnesses, underscored the immense challenges faced in the earthquake response.

JP Morgan's head of investment banking, Daniel Pinto, has indicated that hundreds to thousands of staff may be relocated from London to Dublin, Frankfurt, and Luxembourg in the event of a no-deal Brexit, while the impact on UK staff for Standard Chartered would be "minimal." Other financial institutions, such as Goldman Sachs, Barclays, and insurers Lloyd's of London and Royal London, have announced similar plans to move staff out of London to maintain their European operations.

Law enforcement disbursed a crowd of 150 in the suburb of Ferguson following a disturbance after curfew, which came after the shooting of black teenager Michael Brown by a white police officer. The shooting and subsequent rioting caused nationwide dismay and allegations of police brutality, with seven arrests made during a protest. US civil rights leader Al Sharpton has planned a peaceful rally led by Brown's family. The police named the officer involved, Darren Wilson, who has been on paid administrative leave. The US justice department is investigating the shooting, with the officer being a six-year police veteran with no previous complaints. The release of CCTV footage showing Brown and the officer in a store encounter before the shooting was criticized by Brown's family as an attempt to justify the incident.

Diane Abbott, the Labour Shadow Home Secretary, accuses Theresa May of allowing a reduction in police officer numbers during her tenure as Home Secretary, which she claims could have contributed to recent terror attacks and emphasizes the need for an increase in community police officers. The Conservatives counter that Diane Abbott's views on security are "dangerous" and note that armed police numbers have increased, but the former terrorism law watchdog, Lord Carlile, disputes the connection between the cuts and terrorism, stating that the issue is not about lack of funding for the security services.

The world champions, New Zealand, routed Wales 46-6 in the final Test, marking their 29th consecutive loss to the All Blacks, and their heaviest defeat since 2007. Despite the loss, coach Warren Gatland sees lessons and improvements for his team, particularly in areas like counter-attacking and collision dominance at the breakdown. Steve Hansen suggests that Wales' poor performance may have been influenced by the end of their season, and believes they will rebound in the Six Nations.

Five people, including a 17-year-old British boy named Stephen Thomas who was a talented photographer and had Down's Syndrome, a retired Canadian navy engineer named Jack Slater, and a British woman named Katie Taylor, died in a boat accident in Canada. The accident occurred on the Leviathan ll boat, and all five victims were on the open, upper deck and were not wearing life jackets. The Canadian government is investigating the cause of the accident, and more people could have died had it not been for the quick response from local residents. A 27-year-old Australian man is still missing, and the Down's Syndrome Association, Isambard Community School, and Microsoft paid tribute to Stephen Thomas. The Leviathan ll boat has also been involved in a previous accident in 1998 that killed two people.

The article summarizes that President Thein Sein view the newly signed deal as an opening for "future peace" in Myanmar, but not all major rebel groups, including the United Wa State Army (UWSA) and the Kachin Independence Organisation (KIO), have signed the agreement after two years of negotiations. The government hopes this marks a first step in resolving decades-long conflicts and reaching political settlements, despite some concerns that peace might be short-lived due to the military's potential non-compliance with ceasefires. Formal political discussions for a new form of government will begin in the following months, with the door open for the remaining non-signatory groups to join the process. Aung San Suu Kyi, the opposition leader, was not present at the signing ceremony.

Facebook was ordered by the High Court in Northern Ireland to remove a page that exposed personal information and harassed a man with 15 convictions for sexual offences committed in the 1980s, due to the risk of infringing his human rights. However, the ruling does not suppress information about the man that is already in the public domain, and further steps are required from Facebook to prevent unlawful conduct against the man pending the substantive trial. The judge emphasized that each case of this nature will be sensitive to the specific facts presented.

Apple's unsolicited email to publishers invites them to join a new service, implying agreement to the terms unless they opt out, which requires them to cover Apple in legal issues, allows Apple to place ads beside their content, and does not pay them for using their RSS feeds. Some publishers express concern about being bound by the agreement without actively consenting to it. The terms are considered unusual but not unusual in terms of industry standards, according to a law firm. Apple will launch the app later in 2015 as part of its marketing department and will use human editors instead of algorithms.

The article discusses the concerns among the 165,000 civilians living on Guam, a US territory and important strategic US airbase, following North Korean threats. Governor Eddie Baza Calvo has reassured the public of no immediate threat, but residents are preparing for possible escalation due to the island's proximity to North Korea and the volatile rhetoric between Kim Jong-un and President Trump. Some, however, remain unperturbed, viewing the situation as repetitive.

Sentinel-1b, launched by a Soyuz rocket in French Guiana, will work in conjunction with Sentinel-1a to deliver radar imagery for Earth-monitoring applications such as shipping lane pollution, iceberg surveillance, and land subsidence analysis. The European Union's flagship space project, Copernicus, will utilize this data for a wide range of services including air quality updates, crop monitoring, water resource management, and transport infrastructure planning. Sentinel-1b's commissioning is expected to take three weeks, with four other satellites, including the French space agency's Microscope fundamental physics experiment, also put in orbit during the same launch.

The article suggests that the pound has recently strengthened because market watchers think Theresa May will win a larger majority in the upcoming snap election, which would give her more political leverage to pursue a softer Brexit. This perceived chance for a more favorable Brexit agreement has boosted the pound, however the stock market is down due to the strengthening pound reducing the value of foreign earnings for UK companies. The election is seen as providing more political stability, with businesses generally supportive, but there is uncertainty about whether May will actually pursue a softer Brexit.

A hiker named Pavlina Pizova got lost during a hiking trip on the Routeburn track in Fiordland National Park and spent nearly a month alone in the wilderness after her partner, Ondrej Petr, died following a slip on an ice slope. She was found "ecstatic" and in reasonable health after being spotted by a search team and later interviewed by police.

A Russian family of three, led by Elena, lives paycheck to paycheck and is struggling with over 1 million roubles in debt due to a historical pattern of borrowing dating back to the 1990s, exacerbated by easy credit access and a lack of financial education and contingency planning, evidenced by millions across Russia facing similar hardships.

James Holmes, accused of killing 12 and wounding 58 in a mass shooting at a Batman movie premiere, is facing court proceedings with ongoing mental health and media access concerns. The court has denied media requests for expanded coverage, with Holmes' lawyers objecting and his first court appearance being filmed despite their objections. Holmes appeared dazed in court, prompting speculation about his mental state and calls from victims' family members to avoid using his name and photos. Official investigation of Holmes' apartment revealed 30 grenades and several gallons of gasoline in a booby-trap. While dozens are still recovering in hospital, Batman star Christian Bale visited victims at the Medical Center of Aurora. The shooting has reignited calls for a ban on high-capacity gun magazines, but with elections approaching in November, no near-future action on gun control is expected. A pregnant woman who escaped the cinema shootings gave birth to a baby boy.

The Art Recovery Group is combating the increase in illegally smuggled antiquities from Syria, highlighting the use of visual recognition software and database tracking to identify and recover stolen art, with the ultimate goal of reducing funding for terrorist groups like ISIS that profit from this trade.

The Nuclear Accident Independent Investigation Commission's report found that the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant disaster was a man-made disaster resulting from collusion between government, regulators, and plant operator Tepco, as well asdeep-rooted cultural issues, organizational problems, poor emergency response, and regulator and operator failures. The report criticized the lack of preparedness, prioritization of nuclear energy over public safety, ambiguity in responsibilities, and the failure to effectively address predictable risks, causing confusion, prolonged radiation exposure, and ongoing health and welfare issues for evacuees. The report emphasized that superficial changes would fail to solve the systemic issues at the core of the disaster.

The government's auto-enrolment programme, aimed at ensuring employees save for retirement, has seen a high compliance rate among small businesses with 95% compliance and 66% of employees enrolled. However, challenges remain, including concerns over insufficient contributions and trust management issues, as the minimum contribution rates are set to rise in the coming years.

The article, published in Nature Geoscience, highlights a new calculation by a Canadian-led team that estimates a significant amount (equivalent to Earth's entire land surface covered in a layer 180m deep) of water is stored in the top 2km of the Earth's surface, with only 6% being categorized as "modern" groundwater, which is the most vulnerable and useful to human consumption due to its quick renewal rate and sensitivity to climate change and human contamination. The study further emphasizes the importance of managing this modern groundwater in a sustainable and global perspective, as they are unevenly distributed and finite.

The European Professional Club Rugby announced that Edinburgh will host the finals of both the Champions Cup and the Challenge Cup in 2017, creating a major sporting weekend in Scotland. Event Scotland and the Scottish Government supported the bid, with the new Grand Stade de Lyon to host the French finals the same weekend.

Edward Snowden, whose passport has been cancelled by the US due to leaking information about US surveillance programs, is currently seeking temporary asylum in Russia but remains in the Moscow airport's transit zone. His legal representative stated that Snowden is anxious about leaving the airport and wants to study Russian culture. The White House has expressed a desire for clarity regarding Snowden's status and has urged Russia to extradite him to face espionage charges.
